232320: A reflected XSS vulnerability was discovered in the Stack Trace of the Informatica Cloud documentation website. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by injecting malicious code into the Stack Trace, which would be executed when the page is loaded by a victim. The vulnerability was fixed by disabling the Stack Trace on the affected resource.
232371: An arbitrary file reading vulnerability was discovered in the Informatica Cloud ActiveVOS system. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to read any file on the system by using a double URL encoding technique in the query.
232378: The website was vulnerable to SQL injection due to improper input sanitization in the `███████` parameter of `https://█████████/██████`. This allowed attackers to execute SQL queries on the server, potentially leading to unauthorized access to confidential information and remote code execution. The vulnerability has since been remediated.
277380: The application on an Airforce subdomain was vulnerable to SQL Injection due to insufficient validation on user input, allowing an attacker to execute SQL queries and potentially expose sensitive information. The vulnerability was caused by the lack of proper sanitization of ' characters in the `███=` parameter.
348090: The identity and affiliation commands in Fabric-ca can be manipulated to delete identities or affiliations in a server, even if the server has enabled the allowremove flag. This is because the code for deleting identity and affiliation gets the values from the URL path, which is not protected by signature. A hacker can manipulate the method from other to DELETE and delete all identities or affiliations if they get the request data.
389250: An IDOR vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to the barcode and expiration date of other meal cards by changing the value in a parameter. This resulted in an information disclosure risk. The suggested mitigation was to restrict access to meal cards that the user is not authorized to access.
409237: An IDOR vulnerability was found in a web application that allowed an attacker to access other user accounts by changing the email parameter to a valid email address. This resulted in the disclosure of the name and surname of the affected user. The suggested mitigation action is to follow the Insecure Direct Object Reference Prevention Cheat Sheet.
410334: An XSS and Blind OS command injection vulnerability was discovered due to incorrect handling of characters in the email GET and POST parameters. This allowed an attacker to inject custom Javascript code and execute commands, potentially stealing information and redirecting users to malicious websites. The vulnerability was reported to and remediated by IBM.
496360: An email spoofing vulnerability was found where attackers could forge the sender address of Khan Academy emails. This allowed malicious emails to be sent that appeared to come from Khan Academy's domain. The issue was reported to be due to a lack of email authentication and spoofing protections. Recommended remediations included improving the mail server security filters and enabling DMARC anti-spoofing policies.
506412: An attacker could cause a denial-of-service (DoS) attack on any node client application using the fabric-ca-node SDK by enrolling to a Certificate Authority (CA) that returns an empty response during enrollment. This would trigger an uncaught exception in the event emitter on 'end', causing the containing node process to exit.
532836: A universal cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in the Exness trading app for Android. The vulnerability allowed third-party apps to load any URL in the app's internal webview, leading to the theft of user cookies, including those of the payment system. This could be exploited to execute malicious JavaScript and steal sensitive information.
537047: An open redirection vulnerability was discovered in the login page of a website, allowing an attacker to redirect users to a malicious website by manipulating the "next" parameter in the URL. This could be exploited for phishing attacks and other malicious purposes.
545136: HTTP PUT method was enabled on downloader.ratelimited.me web server, allowing an attacker to upload arbitrary content to the server and potentially compromise other users or the server itself.
615672: A vulnerability was discovered in the algorithm collaborator that allowed an attacker to run JavaScript in the victim's browser by sending a specially crafted websockets request. The vulnerability was caused by unencoded HTML and JavaScript being sent through the TogetherJS library, which is responsible for websockets.
631589: A web cache poisoning attack was discovered that allowed attackers to access user information such as email, name, and member ID. The vulnerability occurred when a logged-in user visited a website, and the server stored the information in the cache, which could then be accessed by a non-logged-in user visiting the same website. The attack could be carried out even in private mode.
671406: The vulnerability allowed an attacker to take over any priceline.com user's account by creating a Google Gsuite account with a domain that matched the victim's email address. The backend of priceline.com did not verify whether the provided email was a confirmed one, enabling the attacker to gain access to the victim's account.
671935: A vulnerability in LibreOffice allowed for a specially crafted file uploaded to Slack to permit local file access and expose an internal Slack AWS credential for the container used to process these files. The vulnerability was fixed on August 13th, 2019, and was documented in CVE-2019-17400.
684268: A stored XSS vulnerability was found in the admins page of GitLab. The vulnerability allowed a malicious administrator to execute stored JavaScript code on behalf of another user's session, which could lead to the theft of the CSRF token and other sensitive information. The vulnerability was caused by the lack of validation of the URL input field for Grafana dashboard, which allowed arbitrary JavaScript to be entered.
684544: A hardcoded front-end code in algo debugger allowed an attacker to execute cross-site scripting (XSS) on algorithm collaborator. The XSS was possible due to unsanitized HTML in the hardcoded expression. The attacker could store the malicious code in the algorithm and share it, causing XSS to fire on anyone who cloned and ran the algorithm.
688546: Clickjacking is a vulnerability that allowed attackers to trick web users into clicking on something different from what they perceived they were clicking on, potentially revealing confidential information or taking control of their computer while clicking on seemingly innocuous web pages. This was possible when websites allowed content to be embedded within a frame, and an attacker could invisibly load the target website into their own site and trick users into clicking on links they never intended to. The vulnerability could be mitigated by adding an X-FRAME-OPTIONS header.
708123: Unescaped characters in the 'dataset owner' field of the custom dataset dashboard allowed for the storage of arbitrary JavaScript, potentially leading to the execution of malicious code and the theft of other users' algorithms.
711662: Default credentials were used on a web application, allowing anyone to log in and perform any action that a regular user could do. The vulnerability was discovered and reported.
712321: The xmlrpc.php file could be used for portscanning or brute force attacks, making it a security vulnerability. It is recommended to disable or hide this file to prevent such attacks.
715740: Sensitive user information was being disclosed due to a researcher's email being added to a group that received new user access requests. The cause of the issue was unknown and there were no known steps to reproduce it. The vulnerability could potentially expose users' organization, phone number, and email address.
723044: A SQL injection vulnerability was found in a website, allowing an attacker to manipulate SQL statements sent to the MySQL database and inject malicious SQL statements. The vulnerability was confirmed using sleep SQL queries with various arithmetic operations. The attacker could change the logic of SQL statements executed against the database.
733072: A path traversal vulnerability in GitLab package registry API allowed an attacker to write any file at any location writable to user git in a GitLab server, leading to remote code execution. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to overwrite critical files related to server access, such as authorized_keys of git user, and gain shell access to the server.
743953: Private objects of other projects could be stolen via project import in GitLab. An attacker could transfer issues, merge requests, and other objects of another project to the imported project by importing a crafted GitLab export. The vulnerability was caused by the fact that many attributes (foreign key) were not excluded during import, allowing the attacker to modify relations between objects and access random resources of other users by traversing the incremental ID space.
745171: Sensitive documents, emails, and credentials were exposed due to the lack of authentication on the test/integration API of a web services provider. An attacker could upload, modify, or delete documents, access and modify email templates, and view all emails sent by the system, including activation codes needed to create a new account and access the proposal system. The vulnerability could have been mitigated by implementing bearer token authentication or restricting access to the API endpoint.
753375: A vulnerability was found that allowed users to upload profile photos to any folder with any file extension. The issue was resolved.
763177: A vulnerability existed in the file attachment feature of the affected software, which allowed users to link non-public file attachments, leading to file disclosure on edit by higher-privileged user. This could result in the disclosure of private file attachments when a user with access to the attachment edits a post of a user without access to it.
766875: The login API was vulnerable to brute force attacks, allowing unauthorized access to accounts. Through exploiting weaknesses in input validation and rate limiting, valid credentials could be obtained, enabling account takeover.
767770: Private objects were exposed through a project import vulnerability, allowing an attacker to modify relations between objects and potentially access random resources of other users by traversing the incremental ID space. The vulnerability was a bypass of a previous fix that blocked all "_ids" attributes.
771215: A blind SQL injection vulnerability was found in a website that allowed an attacker to alter back-end SQL statements by manipulating user input. The vulnerability was confirmed using sleep SQL queries with various arithmetic operations, causing the server to sleep for various amounts of time depending on the result of the arithmetic operation. The impact of the vulnerability was that an attacker could manipulate SQL statements sent to the MySQL database and inject malicious SQL statements, changing the logic of SQL statements executed against the database. The fix for the vulnerability was to filter metacharacters from user input.
783191: The vulnerability allowed for clickjacking attacks on websites that did not have an X-FRAME-OPTIONS header, potentially revealing confidential information or taking control of a user's computer. Attackers could embed content within a frame and trick users into clicking on links they did not intend to. The recommended mitigation was to add an X-FRAME-OPTIONS header.
799839: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found in the email input field of the user profile update feature. The input was not sanitized, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code and execute it on the target application. The vulnerability was exploited by injecting a payload that triggered an alert pop-up. Sanitizing input fields or encoding/escaping special characters is recommended to prevent such vulnerabilities.
799855: A Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability was found in a target endpoint that allowed an attacker to delete an authenticated user's account by tricking them into visiting a malicious website or link. The vulnerability was due to the lack of a CSRF token to verify the authenticity of the user's request.
799895: A CSRF vulnerability was found in a web application that allowed an attacker to modify a user's account settings, including their username, email, and password, with just one click from the user. The vulnerability did not require any user interaction and could result in an account takeover. Mitigation actions suggested include adding a CSRF token to check if the user is authorized to perform the action.
800608: An IDOR vulnerability was found in deleting users' saved projects. An attacker could change the search ID in the URL of a GET request to delete saved projects for any user. This could lead to the deletion of all users' saved searches through brute-forcing their IDs. Mitigation measures should be taken to verify the legitimacy of the user deleting the saved searches.
801370: A remote code execution vulnerability was found in Hyperledger Fabric SDK for Java version 2.0.0 and earlier, due to the lack of configuration of its YAML parser to prevent the instantiation of arbitrary types, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary code.
801437: Sensitive information about the server's configuration was exposed through the .bash_history file at a specific URL on the server.
817331: The login page of a certain URL had weak/auto fill password credentials (admin/admin), which allowed an attacker to gain full access to the super admin panel and make major configuration changes to the services.
822262: A path traversal vulnerability was discovered in the Nuget package registry of GitLab-EE. This allowed an attacker to create any file with an extension “.nupkg” in the filesystem, which could be used to read sensitive files in a GitLab instance. The vulnerability was caused by a path traversal issue in the metadata_extraction_service.rb file, which extracted the uploaded nupkg for the contained nuspec file. An attacker could upload a malicious nupkg file with a crafted XML file that contained a path traversal payload.
837328: A vulnerability existed on quantopian.com that allowed an attacker to perform various POST requests on the website as a different user. The vulnerability was due to excessive control of the victim's UI over the algorithm collaboration feature, which allowed the attacker to force the victim to issue malicious POST requests. By chaining two features together, the attacker could perform any POST request on the website, excluding those that required knowledge of passwords or private strings. The impact of the vulnerability included the ability to rename a user, disable email notifications, delete public posts, and comment on existing topics on behalf of the victim.
838510: Password enforcement for link shares can be bypassed when federated sharing is enabled in Nextcloud 18.0.3, allowing registered users to access shared files without the required password. Additionally, the use of link IDs in federated sharing makes it vulnerable to brute-force attacks, and a potential database breach could expose all federated shares.
838817: The crossdomain.xml file on https://vdc.mtnonline.com/ was insecurely configured, allowing anyone to receive content from the website and potentially steal CSRF tokens and user PII.
846389: An open redirect vulnerability was found in mc-beta-cloud-acronis.com, which allowed attackers to redirect users to malicious websites. The vulnerability was caused by a lack of input validation in the "state" parameter of the authorization URL.
860939: An SSRF vulnerability was discovered on LINE Social Plugins that allowed attackers to bypass DNS verification and access HTML pages through the HTTP protocol. The vulnerability was limited to HTTP/HTML communication and has since been fixed.
864489: A vulnerability in Slack's Workspace creation process allowed an attacker to obtain metadata about Slack's Enterprise customers by submitting the Organization's email domain. The response from the Slack API contained data about the Organization, such as its SSO provider, Enterprise ID, and the email address used to manage their Slack account.
864712: Sensitive customer information, including mobile numbers, names, food orders, and order IDs, was disclosed through customer care recordings that were uploaded to a Google Drive page accessible through a link on a website. The recordings were found in a folder labeled "recordings" and were uploaded on May 1st.
881557: A vulnerability in Slack's PDF viewer allowed for stored cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. Attackers could upload a malicious PDF file containing special characters that could be executed as JavaScript code in the browser, potentially exposing user data. The issue was resolved by patching a vulnerable dependency in the PDF viewer. No customers were impacted by this vulnerability.
889041: Multiple ads hosted on a website were vulnerable to DOM XSS, allowing an attacker to run arbitrary JavaScript under the website's origin. This could be used to add malicious or inappropriate content to the website or takeover the ads seen there. The vulnerability was caused by the injection of the containing page into a JavaScript single quote string, which could be escaped to call the JavaScript alert function.
896338: A misconfiguration in the build environment of Monero Wallet GUI allowed for a DLL preloading attack. Specifically, the application tried to dynamically load certain DLLs that were not present in its directory, causing the system to search for them in other directories such as Windows root and %PATH%. An attacker with write permission to any of these directories could exploit this vulnerability to gain arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation.
917946: A vulnerability existed in Rocket.Chat versions up to 3.3.3 that allowed any authenticated user with only "View Private Room" permission to elevate their privileges to admin and gain access to the server's permissions matrix and Direct Messages. This vulnerability has been fixed in version 5.0 and above.
924151: The Rocket.Chat Desktop app was vulnerable to remote code execution due to insecure use of Electron's `shell.openExternal()` function. Insufficient filtering on the URLs passed to the function allowed an attacker to craft and send a link that, when clicked, executed malicious code from a remote origin on the user's system. The vulnerability was present in multiple releases of the app and was patched by implementing an allowlist for safe protocols.
924851: An XSS vulnerability was found on developers.mtn.com that allowed an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser. The vulnerability was triggered by injecting malicious code into a hidden input field on a form.
943737: Rocket.Chat-Desktop versions prior to v3.0.0-develop are affected by an arbitrary file read vulnerability. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to read arbitrary files on the victim's system by setting up a malicious server and tricking the victim into connecting to it.
948345: A broken authentication session token bug was found in a website, allowing an attacker to reset a victim's password if they have access to the victim's email and the victim forgets to log out of their account on a shared device. The reset password token does not expire after the victim changes their password.
955606: A XSS vulnerability was found on larksuite.com due to the reflection of user-supplied data without appropriate HTML escaping or output encoding in the "back_uri" parameter. This could allow an attacker to inject and execute a Javascript payload in the victim's browser. The vulnerability has been resolved.
963155: An arbitrary file download vulnerability was discovered in WebTorrent, which allowed attackers to smuggle malicious files onto the client's machine by bypassing WebTorrent validation. This could lead to client-side remote code execution and cross-site scripting attacks. The vulnerability was tested on Brave browser version 1.12.114 Chromium: 84.0.4147.135 on Windows OS.
968165: Sensitive customer information, including order details, could be disclosed through the Shopify chat application due to a vulnerability that allowed unauthorized access to the data. Attackers could retrieve order information by brute-forcing the order ID and email address, potentially exposing customers' personal and financial data.
968174: A vulnerability was discovered in the Shopify chat application that allowed an attacker to retrieve the name and ID of a staff member and send messages as if they were the staff member. This could potentially lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information.
968328: A reverse tab-nabbing flaw in WebTorrent allowed attackers to redirect users to malicious torrent files or websites by exploiting the anchor tag that opens files directly from the browser. This could result in victims downloading malicious files or being redirected to harmful webpages. The vulnerability was tested on Brave browser version 1.12.114 Chromium: 84.0.4147.135 on Windows.
970869: Arbitrary requests could be sent through Jupyter Notebooks on GitLab.com and self-hosted GitLab instances, allowing an attacker to send GET/POST/PUT/DELETE requests with an arbitrary payload to targets within the CSP on GitLab.com or arbitrary targets on self-hosted GitLab instances on behalf of the victim. The vulnerability required user interaction in the form of a single click.
971590: The Sony endpoint was vulnerable to Local File Inclusion (LFI) and Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities. The LFI vulnerability was used to read sensitive files, and the SSRF vulnerability was used to view EC2 instance metadata and execute a reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack.
975428: A vulnerability was discovered in the programming education service, LINE entry, where creators were able to share their creations without permission by exploiting an unreleased feature that was still under development.
975514: An arbitrary file download vulnerability was discovered in WebTorrent due to bad handling of redirects. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to force a user to download a malicious file or redirect them to a malicious website. The vulnerability was tested on Brave browser version 1.12.114.
979787: A vulnerability was discovered that allowed unauthorized access to all attachments imported from HackerOne reports with GitLab's automation. This included proofs of concept for unpatched vulnerabilities and was classified as a critical severity finding.
994612: An informational vulnerability was found in the ticket raising system used by Informatica, allowing unauthorized personnel to view certain details about open bugs or project information without login. This could potentially lead to misuse of the disclosed information by an attacker.
995144: A Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) misconfiguration vulnerability was found on a website, allowing an attacker to record personal information of logged-in users who visit the attacker's website. The vulnerability was exploited by sending a GET request with an Origin header to the vulnerable website, which responded with Access-Control-Allow-Origin and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials headers set to the attacker's domain. An exploit was created using an XMLHttpRequest to send the victim's personal information to the attacker's server.
998457: A vulnerability was discovered in the CORS rules of a system that allowed an attacker to execute certain functions on behalf of another user. This was possible due to a CSRF token bypass that was made possible by using the `GET` method to query the GraphQL interface. The issue was resolved by restricting the GraphQL interface to only accept traffic over `POST` and limiting the scope of the CORS rules.
1015283: A vulnerability was discovered in the Shopify online store platform that allowed third-party websites to obtain preview links to a store owner's actions without requiring a password. This was due to the Referrer preview link being leaked to third-party sites, which could be used by someone with control over the third-party site to access the store owner's actions. The vulnerability was resolved by adding a simple HTML code to prevent sending referrer headers to third-party websites.
1018489: An external login service could be connected to an unverified email address on accounts.shopify.com, allowing an attacker to create a backdoor account and potentially gain access to sensitive information. This vulnerability was due to a flaw in the verification process.
1029238: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a website's authentication page via a hidden parameter that was not sanitized. An attacker could inject malicious code into the page and execute it on a victim's browser. The impact of such an attack could include executing malicious scripts, phishing, and defacing the website. The suggested mitigation is to sanitize user inputs and remove any unnecessary parameters.
1029243: A Reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a website via a hidden parameter that was not sanitized. An attacker could inject malicious code through the parameter and execute it on the victim's browser. The impact of such a vulnerability could be significant, including executing malicious scripts, phishing, and defacing the website. The suggested mitigation includes sanitizing user inputs and removing unnecessary parameters.
1032610: A vulnerability was discovered in Twitter's link blocking approach that allowed attackers to post links to blocked domains in tweets. By using a chain of two open redirects and an Ideographic Full Stop in place of the ASCII period, attackers could redirect users to the forbidden domain without being shown any Twitter interstitial page. The impact of this vulnerability was that attackers could post arbitrary unsafe links in tweets.
1033253: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found in ████████ due to unsanitized single quote, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the client browser and perform malicious actions. The suggested mitigation is to sanitize single quotes.
1049402: A PHP Info file at https://radio.mtn.bj/info exposed sensitive information, including passwords, application keys, and email credentials.
1051373: An XSS vulnerability was found on reddit.com via the URL path, allowing an attacker to inject malicious code into the website and potentially steal user data or perform other malicious actions. The vulnerability has since been addressed.
1058427: A reflected XSS vulnerability was discovered on imgur.com, which allowed an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code in the victim's browser by manipulating the "redirect" parameter in a POST request. This could potentially lead to the theft of sensitive information or the compromise of the victim's account.
1059758: A lack of rate limiting in the forgot password functionality of a website allowed an attacker to perform a full account takeover by brute-forcing the password reset code. The vulnerability could be exploited if the attacker had a valid email address associated with the victim's account.
1061736: Personal information of users on a website was disclosed through a critical endpoint, allowing unauthorized access to user accounts. Attackers could use this information to take over any account on the website. The vulnerability was exploited by visiting a link that disclosed the user's personal information, then using a forgot password link to enter the email address and a specific pin to change the password and take over the account.
1066203: An Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerability was discovered in GraphQL that allowed someone with prior Admin access to a Stripe account to add a co-founder to a Stripe Atlas application belonging to the merchant account they used to administer. The issue has been addressed by only allowing the addition of co-founders to Atlas applications by an authorized user.
1072868: A stored XSS vulnerability existed in the GitLab open API viewer due to the use of an old version of swagger-ui that allowed an attacker to inject any HTML elements with any attributes (except script tag) on the page. The vulnerability could be triggered by any user who opened the page and clicked anywhere on the page, and could potentially be used to steal user credentials or take over the victim's account. The vulnerability has since been fixed.
1073780: An ESI injection vulnerability was discovered on a specific endpoint that allowed for the extraction of session cookies with the HttpOnly flag. This vulnerability was chained with a Reflected XSS vulnerability on another endpoint to steal session cookies and take over user accounts. The vulnerability was triggered by a victim clicking on a malicious link.
1081137: An incorrect authorization check vulnerability was found in the `/include/findusers.php` script in ImpressCMS version 1.4.2. Unauthenticated attackers could access the script by providing a valid security token, which could lead to an information disclosure about the CMS users.
1081145: A SQL injection vulnerability was found in the `/include/findusers.php` script of ImpressCMS version 1.4.2. Unsanitized user input passed through the "groups" POST parameter was used to construct a SQL query without proper validation, allowing remote attackers to read sensitive data from the "users" database table through boolean-based SQL Injection attacks. This could potentially lead to full account takeovers.
1081167: Arbitrary cookies could be read and written on Shopify checkout pages via the Google Analytics integration. The postMessage handler on the shop domain did not validate the event.origin before processing events, allowing a malicious webpage to send messages which eventually resulted in function calls on the ga object. It was then possible to write arbitrary cookie values via document.cookie injection, and register an additional GA tracker to read any cookie value. This was only exploitable on shops that had a configured Google Analytics integration.
1081878: Arbitrary file deletion was possible via Path Traversal in the `image-edit.php` script of ImpressCMS version 1.4.2. The vulnerability allowed authenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files, potentially leading to a Denial of Service (DoS) condition or destruction of users data.
1081986: An authentication bypass vulnerability was found in ImpressCMS version 1.4.2. The vulnerability was located in the `/plugins/preloads/autologin.php` script, which allowed an attacker to bypass the authentication mechanism and login as any user without the knowledge of the relative password. This was due to an unsafe way of comparing user input parameters, which used the comparison operator `!=` instead of `!==`.
1083734: A stored XSS vulnerability was found on the "www.intensedebate.com/extras-widgets" page, specifically on the "Recent comments by" module. The vulnerability was caused by a lack of filtration/encoding for special symbols used in blog/site URLs, which allowed an attacker to inject and run arbitrary code on the user page who posted a comment on a malicious blog/site. This could potentially lead to malicious requests being made from the user's account or interaction with the user's personal data. The affected areas should have been filtered/escaped before rendering on the front-end.
1083922: An information disclosure vulnerability was discovered in ShopifyPlus that allowed users with User management access to retrieve the full name of any existing Shopify ID account by email lookup. The vulnerability was reported and has since been resolved.
1084638: An improper access control vulnerability was discovered in Shopify Plus that allowed a Shopify Plus admin to retrieve personally identifiable information (PII) of a user outside their organization. The vulnerability was triggered when the admin attempted to assign a role to a user in another organization, resulting in an error message and an email sent to the admin containing the PII of the user.
1084892: A vulnerability existed where a user with only "Store Management" permission was able to change user management settings using GraphQL, specifically the ability to enforce/unenforce domain state.
1084904: A vulnerability existed in Shopify Plus that allowed users with "Store Management" permission to perform restricted GraphQL calls, specifically "convertUsersFromSaml" and "convertUsersToSaml", which should have been limited to user management only. This could potentially disable a user's ability to login by unlinking their account with SAML identity provider or linking their account with SAML identity provider, causing issues for the victim.
1084939: A user with Store management permission was able to make an enforceSamlOrganizationDomains call, which should have been limited to users with User Management permission only. This vulnerability allowed low-privileged users to enforce SAML integration with a domain, which should have been restricted.
1085042: An improper access control vulnerability was discovered in Shopify Plus that allowed a user to retrieve sensitive information (2FA status, first name, last name, email address, shop id) of a user in another organization by modifying the `id` parameter in a POST request. Although the response showed an error message, an email was sent to the user with the victim's information.
1085332: A vulnerability was discovered in the Shopify GraphQL API that allowed an attacker to query the `shopApps` endpoint and retrieve a list of all existing apps, including private ones. This could potentially lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information.
1085546: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was found in the product description field of the Handshake plugin enabled Shopify store. An attacker could execute arbitrary JavaScript on the shared domain by adding a malicious script in the product description field.
1087122: An HTML injection vulnerability existed in the packing slip generator of some Shopify stores, allowing customers to alter the content of their and other's orders by injecting code in the e-mail field. This could lead to financial losses for the affected stores and even physical theft of goods.
1087744: An improper deep link validation vulnerability was found in the Shopify mobile application. Attackers could bypass path prefix restrictions by appending "../" to the end of the URI, allowing them to load arbitrary URLs in the application's WebView and potentially compromise the app's integrity. This could be exploited to execute JavaScript code and access the app's sandbox via the EASDK.redirect function.
1088159: A vulnerability in Shopify Plus allowed users to break the permissions waterfall by adding the string "FULL" to a user role edit. This would propagate to all users in the role, giving them full access, even if the role showed partial access. This could result in users having excessive permissions.
1092125: A CORS misconfiguration vulnerability existed in a WordPress website, allowing anyone from any third-party domain to fetch information about registered users without authentication via API. The vulnerability was caused by a lack of proper CORS policy implementation, which allowed two-way interaction with the domain. The vulnerability was fixed by implementing a whitelist of trusted domains.
1092831: A password reset token leak was identified on a third-party website, where the application was found to be leaking the token to third-party sites. This could allow malicious users to use the reset password of a user. The token was leaked via the "Host" header, which could be accessed by an attacker who has control over the third-party site.
1100326: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on *.simperium.com due to a vulnerable version of sockjs library. An attacker could execute malicious code and potentially steal user sessions. The vulnerability has been fixed.
1102546: A vulnerability was discovered where the Google Bucket was publicly listable through the link https://cdn.shopify.com/shop-assets/, allowing anonymous users to access and list all objects in GCP that should have been protected.
1102652: A vulnerability was discovered where the GraphQL call `staffOrderNotificationSubscriptionCreate` was not blocked from staff members with `Settings` permission. This allowed staff members to add email addresses to order notifications without the necessary access scope.
1102660: A staff member with only "Settings" permission was able to delete order notifications using the GID, which should have been restricted to staff members with "Order" permission. This vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to the staff order notification feature.
1102764: Slack's Blocked Previews feature was rendered ineffective due to the lack of URL normalization in the backend. This allowed for easy bypasses of a workspace's list of blocked previews, enabling malicious actors to get their links to preview in Slack regardless of the workspace's list of blocked previews.
1104349: A server-side template injection vulnerability was discovered on Glovoapp's sign-up process. An attacker could inject malicious payloads in the Name field during registration, which would be rendered server-side and executed in the promotional/welcome emails sent to the user. This could potentially lead to sensitive information disclosure and remote code execution.
1122513: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was found on devicelock.com/forum/ that allowed an attacker to inject malicious HTML/JavaScript code into the "City" input field, leading to the execution of arbitrary code in the victim's browser.
1122791: A Remote Code Execution vulnerability was found on a military server due to improper access control to SCORM Zip upload/import. An attacker could upload a SCORM course package containing an ASPX shell that would be extracted onto the server, allowing them to execute commands. This could lead to sensitive information theft, internal system pivoting, and other critical consequences.
1124974: A security vulnerability was found on devicelock.com that allowed an attacker to access any ticket support and read all the information that users sent to the support without user interaction. The attacker could have full access to users' tickets using the ticket ID only.
1125752: The subdomain soa-accp.glbx.tva.gov was vulnerable to SQL injection through the /api/ path, allowing an attacker to manipulate SQL statements and change the logic of SQL statements executed against the database.
1126414: Local authentication (PIN code) on the mobile app was vulnerable to bypass by changing the system time to a value when the lock had not yet been triggered. 1379707: A vulnerability was discovered in the Monero daemon that allowed an attacker to crash any remote node that exposes the `get_output_distribution` function call or tie up availability of that function call, by passing a large list of amounts to the function call. The vulnerability affected all releases of the Monero daemon.
1379975: A chain of five vulnerabilities was discovered that allowed an attacker to gain JIT capabilities and execute arbitrary payloads on PlayStation 4 and PlayStation 5. The vulnerabilities included insecure deserialization, arbitrary class instantiation, permission bypass, write-what-where primitive, and buffer overflow. An attacker could exploit these vulnerabilities to load and execute pirated games, bypass kernel security measures, and cause a kernel panic. The exploit chain was demonstrated in an ISO image called "bd-jb."
1380121: A weak Flask session key was discovered in jarvis-new.urbanclap.com, allowing attackers to modify the session state and log in as any user, resulting in a full compromise of the instance. The vulnerability was fixed by changing the REDASH_COOKIE_SECRET and REDASH_SECRET_KEY to a random value.
1382448: A vulnerability was discovered on the Acronis website that allowed an attacker to launch a DoS attack by using the %0A (new line) command and a limitless URL. The attack caused the site to give a 502 bad gateway error and could be executed by opening multiple pages or using a curl command. The vulnerability was caused by the site allowing very long characters and not limiting the number of characters in the URL.
1382919: An ingress-nginx path vulnerability allowed a user with the permissions to create an ingress resource to obtain the ingress-nginx service account token, which could list secrets in all namespaces (cluster-wide). The vulnerability was caused by a configuration file injection that created a new route to the /gaf path and used an alias that mapped to the /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ directory on the ingress-nginx-controller pod. The vulnerability affected Kubernetes version 1.20 and the nginx ingress controller version 1.0.4.
1386277: Attachment references in markdown did not warn before downloading, allowing an attacker to bypass the functionality of the warning popup and redirect the victim to a third-party website without any warning. This could potentially lead to the attacker obtaining the victim's IP address or tricking them into logging in to a malicious website.
1388788: The Acronis Cloud Manager Admin Portal default swagger UI was vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS), which could have allowed an attacker to target admin users and access sensitive data. The vulnerability was caused by an older version of dom-purify used by the swagger instance.
1390331: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered in the Doctrine/DBAL version used by Nextcloud. The vulnerability allowed for SQL injection via the limit parameter on user-facing APIs, potentially leading to full-fledged SQL injection via user-provided input. The vulnerability was patched in a security advisory.
1390782: A vulnerability was found in a domain pointing to an AWS instance, which could have been taken over by an attacker. The domain contained a record pointing to the instance, but querying for any IP under the instance returned an error. An attacker could have claimed the instance by creating a load balancer with the same name and numbers. This could have allowed the attacker to gain access to the domain and potentially trick users into giving away their credentials through a phishing form.
1391635: The Cloudflare Deception Armor was vulnerable to cache deception attacks due to a flaw in its page rule protection. Attackers could bypass the protection by using a crafted URL with a ".avif" extension, tricking Cloudflare edge to cache sensitive information. The vulnerability has been fixed with an improved page rule.
1392032: Sensitive information about shop's orders could be accessed by a staff with only `Customers` permission, which is a violation of Shopify's documentation that requires `Orders` (`read_orders`) permissions to access shop's orders. This vulnerability could lead to information disclosure.
1392211: A vulnerability in Safari allowed a malicious actor to remotely extract a user's IP address without their consent by preloading a third-party domain. The issue was caused by the use of remote domain links with preconnect, which allowed the attacker to receive a TCP connection and extract the IP and hostname of the victim. This could lead to various attacks, including spear phishing, account takeover, and doxxing. The vulnerability affected macOS and iOS Safari.
1392935: The website was vulnerable to a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack via a crafted X-Forwarded-Host header. An attacker could have exploited this vulnerability to execute malicious scripts in the victim's browser and access sensitive information such as cookies and session tokens. The vulnerability has been mitigated by ignoring invalid browser headers and filtering metacharacters from user input.
1394399: OAuth tokens were leaked in plaintext in the logs of Rocket.Chat, potentially allowing unauthorized access to systems that the tokens grant access to. The vulnerability was fixed in version 4.6.4.
1394984: The email verification process for setting up 2FA in Evernote was vulnerable to brute force attacks. An attacker could brute force the confirmation code, which was only 6 digits long, and set up their own phone number for the victim's account. This would result in the victim being permanently locked out of their account, as they would not receive the 2FA codes.
1397786: The Remedy Single Sign-On (Remedy SSO) Server at remedysso.mtncameroon.net had a default administrator username and password, allowing unauthorized access to the system and sensitive information. The vulnerability was remediated by changing the password of the Admin user or disabling the account.
1397788: Sensitive information, including usernames, encrypted passwords, internal IP addresses, and configuration data of internal services, could be accessed by an attacker through the application's config file. The vulnerability has been remediated by configuring the application to not reveal sensitive information to clients.
1398305: Two XSS sanitization bypasses were discovered in GitLab. The SyntaxHighlightFilter creates HTML from unsanitized data, allowing for a server-side XSS filter bypass. Additionally, the gl-emoji custom element can be used to bypass the GitLab UI v-safe-html directive sanitization on the frontend side by injecting the payload into the name attribute. An attacker who can comment on an issue or other pages where comments can be posted can exploit these vulnerabilities to XSS users who visit that issue or page.
1401268: Rocket.Chat versions 4.1.0 with the 'marked' parser were affected by a persistent CSS injection vulnerability. Due to more loose restrictions in the 'marked' parser, an attacker could inject malicious CSS code into messages, leading to the manipulation of the chat window's style, blocking of functionality, and hijacking of the content of targeted users. The vulnerability was fixed in version 5.0.
1401444: Arbitrary commands could be executed on GitLab servers via the WikiCloth markdown rendering if the `rubyluabridge` gem was installed. This was due to the lua sandbox being escapable using code from the official wiki. A user with the ability to add wiki pages could exploit this vulnerability.
1402249: File and folder names with leading and trailing control characters were not properly filtered in Nextcloud, allowing for the creation of files and folders with such characters. While the server rejected files and folders with control characters in the middle of their names, this could have been an opportunity for injection.
1403614: A vulnerability existed in Nextcloud server versions 22.2.2 and earlier that allowed an attacker to force an admin to install recommended applications without requiring an anti-CSRF token. An attacker could create a malicious page on a controlled domain and trick an admin into visiting it, which would initiate the installation process of recommended applications. The vulnerability has been patched.
1404612: Multiple vulnerabilities were found in the TikTok SMB subdomain, including Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), and XSS, which could have led to account takeover. An attacker could modify the details of another user due to a missing authorization check, and a malicious link could be used to modify a user's email address. The vulnerability has been resolved.
1404770: A stored XSS vulnerability was found in the "product type" field of the Judge.me app in Shopify. An attacker could insert malicious code into the field, which would be executed when a user filters products by type in the app, potentially leading to session hijacking or cookie stealing.
1404804: A XSS vulnerability was found in the email templates of Judge.me, a product review and Q&A platform for Shopify stores. The vulnerability was caused by a custom `onIgnoreTag` function in the `js-xss` library used to prevent XSS on email templates previews. An attacker could bypass this filter and achieve account takeover in 1-click by sending a malicious email template and using HMAC authentication to force another user to preview it. The vulnerability also allowed for private content leak and impersonation on support chat.
1406335: The subdomain images.crossinstall.com pointed to an AWS S3 bucket that no longer existed, allowing an attacker to take control of the domain and serve arbitrary/malicious content to any customers or servers pointing to it. The impact of this subdomain takeover could be high, especially if the domain was whitelisted for OAuth or if there were cookies scoped to the entire domain.
1406495: A vulnerability was discovered in Shopify that allowed an attacker to disable the login attempt of any Shopify owner for 24 hours using a zero-click method. The vulnerability was due to improper security while setting up two-factor authentication via mobile phone. An attacker could change the mobile number associated with the victim's account and then repeatedly tap the "resend code" button until the server blocked the victim's login attempts. This could result in a denial of service for the victim.
1406926: Forced password protection for link and email shares in Nextcloud could be bypassed by a user by creating a circle and adding an email address to it, allowing them to share files without password protection. The vulnerability was present in Nextcloud version 22.2.3 and Circles version 22.1.1.
1406953: Message ID Enumeration was possible through the `actionLinkHandler` method, which allowed MongoDB queries with Regex patterns to be used without proper validation. This vulnerability could be exploited by authenticated attackers to enumerate existing Message IDs on the server. The vulnerability was fixed in versions 4.7.5, 4.8.2, and 5.0.
1408589: Active usernames of registered users in Wordpress were exposed without authentication via API, allowing anyone to view them. This could lead to brute force attacks on these users. The vulnerability was found in the oembed/1.0/embed and author-sitemap.xml paths. Mitigation actions include blocking the active path and disabling or blocking outside access to the XMLRPC.php file.
1408692: Arbitrary sensitive files of the Nextcloud Android app could be leaked through the file upload functionality due to insufficient checks on file paths. The vulnerability allowed attackers to bypass the fix implemented by Nextcloud and access protected/private files. The issue was addressed by disallowing any file whose path has the package name but isn't in the temp or cache folder of Nextcloud.
1408782: An arbitrary amount could be paid against a generated order request to add up to 10K INR to a Zomato wallet without paying the full amount. The vulnerability was limited to the Zomato wallet and did not affect other payment methods or consumers. The issue was fixed after being reported by a researcher.
1409788: Arbitrary POST requests could be made as a victim user from HTML injection in Jupyter notebooks on GitLab.com due to arbitrary data-* attributes not being filtered out by DOMPurify, allowing attackers to hijack GitLab UI JavaScript to make POST requests. This could result in an attacker gaining admin access to the instance or other possible attack vectors.
1410214: A vulnerability was found in Smokescreen, an open source project used to restrict URLs that internal services can connect to, which allowed bypassing of the deny list feature by appending a dot to the end of user-supplied URLs, potentially leading to server-side request forgery (SSRF) attacks.
1410246: A vulnerability in Rocket.Chat versions 3.18.3 and 4.1.2 allowed authenticated users to disclose messages they were mentioned in from private channels and direct messages they should not have access to. The getUserMentionsByChannel meteor server method did not check the user's access permission to the room and returned all messages the user has been mentioned in. The vulnerability was fixed in version 5.0.
1410357: Improper input data validation in the `getUsersOfRoom` Meteor server method allowed authenticated users to enumerate existing rooms and subscribed users. This vulnerability allowed users with access to at least one channel to leak the members of another channel they should not have access to. The vulnerability was fixed in versions 4.7.5, 4.8.2, and 5.0.0 of Rocket.Chat.
1410459: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found in the Shopify Github Integration feature, specifically in the URL https://online-store-git.shopifycloud.com. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute malicious JavaScript code and perform various attacks, such as phishing and data theft. The vulnerability was reported and fixed.
1410498: Sensitive buyer information could be leaked through the Checkout Comments addon in a Shopify store. An attacker could intercept and edit a request to publish a comment, allowing them to view the email address and name of the buyer who left the comment.
1411363: A vulnerability was found in the password creation process of the website, allowing users to set passwords of any length without any limit. This could potentially cause resource consumption on the server and lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack.
1415241: A default password was discovered on IP address 34.120.209.175, allowing unauthorized access to the system. The IP was found to have a SSL certificate pointing to ElasticSearch, and logging in with the default credentials provided access to the system. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to obtain the default password and potentially gain unauthorized access to sensitive information.
1415825: A vulnerability was discovered in Cisco ASA that allowed anyone to read any file present on the server without authentication. The vulnerability could be exploited by visiting a specific URL. Cisco has released a security advisory with mitigation steps.
1416672: A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the question edit feature of Judge.me product reviews. An attacker could create a product or write a question with a malicious script as the name, which would execute when the question is edited in the Shopify admin panel. This could result in the theft of user cookies.
1417211: A vulnerability in Gitlab runner allowed any user with access to Gitlab CI to have root access on the Gitlab Runner server. This was due to the installation of Gitlab runner using Docker-in-Docker, which allowed root access to the server. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to access sensitive data stored in projects running in Gitlab-CI.
1418419: A race condition was found on the /v2/seats endpoint which allowed bypassing the original seat limit.
1418891: Access to the GET `jars/{jar_id}/plan` API endpoint on Apache Flink was not restricted, allowing attackers to load java class files with specified arguments and gain remote code execution on the server.
1419341: A bug in Cloudflare's Email Routing feature allowed for the hijacking of emails sent to any domain that used Cloudflare Email Forwarding. The vulnerability allowed for the redirection of email messages for an unverified zone to a different mailbox and the overwriting of the email forwarding configuration created by the zone owner. The issue has since been fixed by the Engineering team.
1420697: Improper handling of payment methods in the billing page of app.lemlist.com allowed an attacker to bypass the payment and use paid features without paying anything. The vulnerability was exploited by filling in the address tab, choosing Email outreach, increasing the number of seats, and canceling the subscription.
1421345: A link-shortener bypass vulnerability was reported and fixed, but a regression on the fix occurred, allowing the vulnerability to be reproducible with the same payload. The impact of the vulnerability was previously reported.
1421804: The admin dashboard of two subdomains, https://datastories.shopify.com/admin.php and https://data-stories-website.shopifycloud.com/admin.php, were accessible without authentication, allowing unauthorized users to view administrative information. The CSRF token was also exposed, which could potentially lead to a CSRF attack.
1422641: Sensitive information disclosure and modification was possible in an outdated version of Oracle ADF Faces due to wrong settings. Attackers could access and modify personal information such as first name, last name, and phone number. The vulnerability was caused by incorrect settings in the ADF Faces system, which allowed unauthenticated users to view and modify sensitive information.
1423496: A vulnerability (CVE-2021-44228) in log4j allowed for potential arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability could be mitigated by updating log4j or disabling jndi support.
1423704: A vulnerability existed in FetLife that allowed an attacker to determine if a user was a FetLife supporter, even if the user had hidden their support badge in their account privacy settings. The attacker could start a conversation with the victim and then view the JSON response of the conversation to see if the "is_supporter" field was set to true. This vulnerability affected all users except those with "strict" inbox privacy settings.
1425474: The website at nps.acronis.com was vulnerable to CVE-2021-44228, a remote code execution vulnerability in the Apache Log4j library. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by injecting a payload in the request headers, leading to the deserialization of untrusted data and allowing for remote code execution. The vulnerability could be mitigated by updating to the latest version of Log4j or removing the JndiLookup class from the class path.
1425882: A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered on AliExpress Review Importer/Products when deleting a product. An attacker could create a product with a malicious script as the name and then delete it, triggering the script and potentially stealing cookies.
1427086: A path traversal vulnerability was discovered in Grafana 8.x that allowed an unauthenticated user to read arbitrary files on the server by exploiting the vulnerability. This could potentially lead to unauthorized access to sensitive information.
1428207: A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the question edit feature of Judge.me product reviews. An attacker could create a product with a malicious name, then write a question with the same name, and delete the product. When the question is edited in the Shopify admin, the XSS payload is executed, allowing for session stealing.
1429014: A 0-day exploit in the Java package Log4j, identified as CVE-2021-44228, allowed for remote code execution (RCE) on the █████████ domain. The vulnerability was exploited by pasting a specific code on the URL parameter, which sent a reverse ping back to Burp Collaborator. Mitigation and remediation actions were suggested.
1429148: The subdomain "new.rubyonrails.org" was vulnerable to subdomain takeover, as it was pointing to an unclaimed Github Page. This could have allowed an attacker to host malicious content, execute arbitrary javascript code, and steal cookies set to the root domain. The issue was mitigated by removing the DNS record.
1429694: Node.js APIs for reporting certificate fields were ambiguous and allowed bypassing certificate verification in some circumstances, due to the misuse of OpenSSL's printing functions. This could lead to certificate verification bypasses, such as a name-constrained intermediate, and was a generally unsafe pattern. The vulnerability was privately disclosed and a fix was developed and rolled out.
1431042: Prototype pollution was possible via the `properties` parameter of the `console.table` function in Node.js, allowing an attacker to pollute the object prototype with empty strings. This could lead to a denial of service attack.
1434056: A buffer overflow vulnerability was discovered in the mod_lua multipart parser of Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.51 and earlier. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted request body, potentially leading to a denial of service attack. The issue was fixed in version 2.4.52.
1434179: An external link in the Portuguese version of Kubernetes docs referred to a website that was not registered and could be purchased by an attacker to host malicious content or software, potentially leading to remote code execution for users who accessed the page.
1434967: A Github account takeover vulnerability was discovered on the Kubernetes CSI documentation page. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to take over an external Github account linked on the page, which could then be used to host malicious code that could potentially lead to remote code execution.
1436460: A document containing Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) was publicly available on the internet, contrary to DoD standards. The document contained sensitive information and was accessible since around a certain date. The vulnerability has been reported, and the suggested mitigation action is to remove the document from public internet.
1438052: A race condition vulnerability was found in the faucet implementation of Tendermint's Starport. A malicious user could send concurrent requests to fetch more tokens from the faucet than the maximum credit limit allowed, due to a mapping issue in the "Transfer" function.
1438393: A vulnerability was discovered in a log4j library, which could potentially allow for arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability was reported to the Department of Defense and validated by their Vulnerability Disclosure Program team. The affected system owner was notified for resolution.
1439026: A vulnerability in the Twitter Android client allowed anyone to obtain a Twitter ID of any user by submitting a phone number or email, even if the user had prohibited this action in the privacy settings. The bug existed due to the process of authorization used in the Android client of Twitter, specifically in the process of checking the duplication of a Twitter account. This could lead to a loss of privacy for many users.
1439355: A Github account used as a base action in the Shopify Unity Buy SDK repository was taken over by an attacker, who could have hosted a malicious action on it. This would have allowed the attacker to access Shopify's credentials and all private repositories of the organization.
1439552: A vulnerability in GitLab Pages allowed attackers to steal session tokens by intercepting requests to the `/auth` endpoint on a Pages site using service workers. This allowed attackers to access private GitLab Pages sites that the victim had access to. The vulnerability was caused by a lack of validation of `gitlab-pages` session cookies to ensure that the requested subdomain was the same as the subdomain to which the session cookie was issued for.
1439593: Arbitrary files could be read via the bulk imports UploadsPipeline due to the bulk imports API not removing symlinks when untaring the uploads.tar.gz file, allowing any file that the git user has read access to be read and uploaded when importing a group. This could be exploited by a user with access to import a group on GitLab to read arbitrary files on the GitLab server.
1441103: A use-after-free vulnerability in setsockopt IPV6_2292PKTOPTIONS allowed attackers to gain kernel access on the PS5. The vulnerability was exploited in conjunction with the bd-j exploit chain.
1441988: A stored XSS vulnerability was found on the admin dashboard of linkpop.com due to lack of sanitization and client-side protections. Attackers could exploit this vulnerability to execute malicious JavaScript on the victim's behalf, bypass CORS and SOAP, and exfiltrate cookies.
1442017: A self XSS vulnerability was found in the Create New Workspace screen of a website, allowing an attacker to steal user cookies by injecting a payload into the workspace name input field.
1443211: An OTP bypass vulnerability was discovered on a customer portal website, allowing an attacker to use the OTP sent to a victim's email to verify the attacker's email and gain access to the victim's account. The attacker was able to bypass the email verification process and access the account without being logged out by the server.
1443567: An HTML injection vulnerability was found on the website that allowed an attacker to inject HTML code into an email invitation sent to a victim. This could lead to the victim being redirected to a malicious site or tricked into giving away login credentials.
1443654: An information disclosure vulnerability was discovered on the Salesforce Lightning endpoint of disposal.gsa.gov, which allowed an attacker to obtain contact details of registered users by sending a specially crafted POST request to the endpoint. The vulnerability was caused by improper handling of user input and could lead to the exposure of sensitive information.
1444675: The Omise dashboard website was vulnerable to Host Header Injection, which allowed for Open Redirection and Content Spoofing or Text Injection attacks. An attacker could manipulate the X-Forwarded-Host header to redirect users to malicious websites or inject arbitrary text into the website, potentially leading to phishing attacks.
1446090: A vulnerability existed in Krisp's Team plan billing process that allowed an attacker to add more seats by paying less by manipulating the PUT /v2/seats request. By entering a decimal number instead of an integer while adding a seat, the number was rounded up, but the price was only multiplied by the integer part, allowing an attacker to reduce the price by adding and deleting seats.
1446236: A Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in Apereo CAS through version 6.4.1, allowing attackers to inject malicious scripts via POST requests sent to the REST API endpoints. The vulnerability could be exploited by submitting malicious scripts via parameters such as the ticket ID or the username, resulting in the execution of the script. The vulnerability was fixed in versions 6.3.7.4 and 6.4.4.2.
1446767: The `/api/v1/chat.getThreadsList` API route in Rocket.Chat did not sanitize user inputs and could therefore leak private thread messages to unauthorized users via MongoDB injection. An authenticated adversary could provide an input that matches multiple rooms, of which the first match can be read by the malicious user. This vulnerability affected the `develop` branch and previous versions of Rocket.Chat. The issue was fixed in version 5.0.
1447440: The `getRoomRoles` Meteor method in Rocket.Chat versions 4.3.1, 3.18.3, and develop lacked ACL checks, allowing unauthorized clients to query channel members with special roles and leak private channel members' information. The vulnerability was fixed in versions 4.7.5, 4.8.2, and 5.0.0.
1447751: Sensitive Firebase configuration data, including API key and database URL, was disclosed in the source code of a subdomain of mtn.co.ug. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to upload malicious data to the Firebase account of pulseradio.mtn.co.ug and access the database. This could lead to potential misuse of the data and harm the reputation of mtn.co.ug. The issue was resolved by changing the database rule to private.
1448268: Two Factor Authentication (2FA) in Rocket.Chat was vulnerable to bypass when the server was told to use CAS during login. The 2FA Login Handler skipped validation when it found CAS enabled, allowing login to proceed without validation of a second factor. The vulnerability affected versions 4.3.1, 3.18.3, and develop. The issue was fixed in versions 4.7.5, 4.8.2, and 5.0.0.
1448550: An IDOR vulnerability on developers.mtn.com allowed any user to remove any other user from their team by modifying the request with the target user's ID. This vulnerability also resulted in an information disclosure as user and team names were disclosed in the response from the server. The vulnerability was remediated by implementing proper session management, access control mechanisms, and validation of access to team IDs.
1450117: An IDOR vulnerability was found in Nextcloud Deck application version 1.6.0, allowing any user without privilege to add lists with tasks in any user board. The vulnerability was exploited by changing the `boardId` parameter in a PUT request to add a new list with tasks to the victim's board without their knowledge. The impact of the vulnerability was broken access control.
1450368: A vulnerability was discovered in the Android app for Nextcloud Client version 3.18.1 that allowed bypassing the app lock protection by repeatedly opening and closing the app. This could allow unauthorized access to Nextcloud files if an attacker gained physical access to an unlocked Android device with the vulnerable Nextcloud app installed and configured.
1451394: A post-based reflected XSS vulnerability was found in dailydeals.mtn.co.za, which could allow an attacker to steal user cookies, redirect them to arbitrary domains, and perform various attacks. The vulnerability was triggered by submitting a crafted form with a malicious script as a hidden input value.
1454002: A vulnerability allowed any 3rd-party application to retrieve files from the protected directory of the OwnCloud Android application. The issue was caused by an exported activity that accepted URIs of files for upload, which could be exploited to upload any files, including database files, in the context of the OwnCloud app. The vulnerability was mitigated by implementing protections similar to those used in a related intent-filter.
1455248: A buffer overflow vulnerability was discovered in the `CGI.escape_html` method of the Ruby programming language. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to write unintended data to memory by passing a very large string to the method on a platform where the `long` data type takes 4 bytes. The vulnerability was assigned the CVE identifier CVE-2021-41816 and has been fixed in updated versions of the `cgi` gem and Ruby.
1455257: A vulnerability in the web services interface of Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software allowed an unauthenticated, remote attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and read sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper input validation of URLs in HTTP requests processed by an affected device. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request containing directory traversal character sequences to an affected device. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to view arbitrary files within the web services file system on the targeted device. The web services file system was enabled when the affected device was configured with either WebVPN or AnyConnect features. This vulnerability could not be used to obtain access to ASA or FTD system files or underlying operating system (OS) files.
1455266: An arbitrary file deletion vulnerability (CVE-2020-3187) was found on a Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software. An unauthenticated, remote attacker could exploit the vulnerability to conduct directory traversal attacks and obtain read and delete access to sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability has been patched, and users are advised to upgrade to the latest version.
1455411: A vulnerability was found in OpenSSL 3.0.0 SSL/TLS clients that mishandled negative return values from X509_verify_cert(), causing IO functions to not indicate success and SSL_get_error() to return an unexpected value. This could result in incorrect behavior, such as crashes or infinite loops. The issue was made more serious by a separate bug in OpenSSL 3.0 that caused X509_verify_cert() to indicate an internal error when processing a certificate chain. The vulnerability was fixed in OpenSSL 3.0.1.
1455987: The SurveyMonkey SDK used in the Social Trading app for collecting surveys was implemented in an insecure manner, allowing any app installed on the user's device to launch an exported activity. This activity was a fragment that loaded data into a WebView by supplying externally controlled Intent Extras into the loadDataWithBaseURL() method of the WebView, which could be used to steal user's cookies or execute OSRF attacks. This vulnerability could lead to account takeover, compromise of user credentials and data, and unauthorized access to user's open and closed positions, strategies, and portfolios. The vulnerability was fixed by adding exported="false" to the activity.
1457277: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in a website's parameter, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser. The impact of this vulnerability includes potential cookie exfiltration, SOAP bypass, CORS bypass, and executing JavaScript on the victim's behalf. The affected system host and product/version are not disclosed. A proof of concept URL was provided. No CVE number was assigned.
1457413: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered at a specific URL, allowing for potential execution of malicious JavaScript on the victim's behalf and bypassing certain security measures. No affected products or CVE numbers were mentioned, and mitigation or remediation actions were not suggested.
1457444: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in a parameter of a website, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser. The vulnerability could potentially lead to cookies exfiltration, SOAP bypass, CORS bypass, and other malicious actions. No information was provided on affected products or suggested mitigation actions.
1457493: A reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in a parameter of a website, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser. The vulnerability could potentially lead to cookies exfiltration, SOAP and CORS bypass, and other malicious activities. No information was provided on affected products or suggested mitigation actions.
1457546: A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered at a certain URL, allowing for potential execution of malicious JavaScript on the victim's behalf and exfiltration of cookies. No affected products or CVE numbers were specified, and a proof of concept was provided.
1457928: A subdomain of ███████ was vulnerable to a subdomain takeover due to a CNAME pointing to an unclaimed domain. An attacker could have obtained sensitive information from users via phishing, cookie hijacking, or XSS. The suggested mitigation action is to remove the CNAME of the vulnerable subdomain.
1458020: A NoSQL-Injection vulnerability in the `getS3FileUrl` Meteor server method allowed authenticated users to enumerate and access arbitrary file uploads they should not have access to. The vulnerability was fixed in versions 4.7.5, 4.8.2, and 5.0.
1458236: A 0-day Cross Origin Request Forgery vulnerability was discovered in Grafana 8.x hosted on Aiven platforms, allowing an attacker to mount a CSRF attack against authenticated victims of other Grafana instances hosted on `*.aivencloud.com`. The vulnerability was caused by Grafana setting their auth cookie `grafana_session` to `SameSite=Lax; Secure`. No official remediation has been released yet.
1459338: A vulnerability was discovered where a user was able to create a page with the name "/performance_report" using the POST method, while being unable to create a page with the name "/graphql" due to it being reserved. This vulnerability could potentially lead to security issues.
1460373: A race condition vulnerability was found in the `Invite Your Friend to Join FetLife` feature of fetlife.com. 1555015: A vulnerability was discovered in Cisco ASA that allowed unauthenticated users to read any file on the server. The vulnerability was tracked as CVE-2020-3452 and could be exploited by visiting specific URLs. Cisco released a security advisory with mitigation steps.
1555021: A vulnerability (CVE-2020-3452) was discovered in Cisco ASA that allowed unauthenticated users to read any file present on the server by visiting specific URLs. The vulnerability was caused by improper input validation and was patched by Cisco.
1555025: A vulnerability in Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software allowed an unauthenticated attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and obtain read and delete access to sensitive files on a targeted system.
