1555027: A vulnerability in Cisco Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Firepower Threat Defense (FTD) Software allowed an unauthenticated attacker to conduct directory traversal attacks and obtain read and delete access to sensitive files on a targeted system. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper input validation of the HTTP URL. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request containing directory traversal character sequences. The vulnerability could allow the attacker to view or delete arbitrary files on the targeted system.
1555441: A vulnerability was found in Curl that allowed a denial-of-service (DoS) attack if the NSS TLS library was used and the CERTINFO option was enabled. An attacker could use maliciously crafted certificates on a server to make Curl run into an endless loop when connecting to the server. The vulnerability was caused by a bug in the code that counted certificates in the chain received from servers via TLS. The severity of the vulnerability was estimated to be low as it relied on CERTINFO being enabled and NSS being used, which is not that popular and will soon be deprecated.
1555502: Custom apps in Shopify allowed collaborators and staff members to create, edit, and install custom apps for a store. However, a missing permission, "Manage and install apps and channels," was required to manage custom apps. If a staff member was granted permission to only one specific app, they were still able to create, edit, and install custom apps by using API endpoints directly, which was not intended. This vulnerability allowed an attacker to modify existing custom apps, change Admin API scopes, and uninstall or reinstall the app, among other actions.
1555582: RXSS was found on a website, allowing an attacker to perform actions, view information, modify data, and initiate interactions with other users. The vulnerability was caused by a lack of input filtering and output encoding, and could have been mitigated with the use of appropriate response headers and a Content Security Policy.
1555796: A vulnerability existed in Curl that allowed for the reuse of TLS connections without considering security options, potentially resulting in the use of lower security or wrong identity for subsequent connections to the same host. The issue was caused by a failure to consider certain security-related options when reusing TLS connections.
1556808: The ██████ site was found to have exposed its Non-Cloudflare IP, which could allow bypassing of anti-DDoS mechanisms. This could potentially allow attackers to launch DDoS attacks on the servers without being stopped by CloudFlare.
1557449: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-30115) was found in curl that allowed an attacker to bypass HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) checks by using a trailing dot in the URL. This could allow an attacker to load a website over HTTP instead of HTTPS, potentially exposing sensitive information.
1558010: A blind XSS vulnerability was discovered in the PullRequest admin portal via the `/reviews/ratings/{uuid}` endpoint. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to inject a payload into the `Disliked_reviewers`, `Liked_reviewers`, and `Reasons` fields without any encoding, potentially leading to unauthorized access to sensitive information.
1559262: Multiple confirmation_token could be sent in the same request for email verification using an array in the query string, bypassing the rate limit of 100 req/10 minutes. The vulnerability could have made the confirmation_token slightly easier to guess, but it would still have required more than a billion years to brute-force the confirmation token using a single IP. A patch has been released to address the vulnerability.
1560717: Restricted files on Phabricator could be made public via Diffusion, as Phabricator did not check if the user had access to the file before allowing it to be attached in commit messages. This allowed an attacker to gain access to restricted file objects by enumerating and including the file syntax in the commit message.
1561377: A Django application running with debug mode enabled was discovered to disclose sensitive system and configuration details. When exceptions occurred, detailed error pages were displayed containing metadata such as Django settings, database credentials, file paths and code snippets. Disabling debug mode by setting DEBUG=False in the settings file prevents such information leaks.
1562515: An integer overflow vulnerability was discovered that allowed attackers to manipulate the quantity value and change the price of items during the "cash on delivery" option. This could result in price manipulation and potentially financial loss.
1563139: The global default settings page in Phabricator was accessible to non-administrators, allowing any user to modify certain settings that could disrupt the installation, such as the accessibility theme, language, and notifications. The vulnerability was fixed in a previous update.
1563142: A vulnerability was discovered in Slowvote and Countdown objects that allowed for a Denial of Service attack due to recursive inclusion. By including the object's own ID in the description, it would recursively include and prevent the page from loading, causing a Denial of Service.
1563334: A One Click XSS vulnerability was discovered in Shopify's website that allowed attackers to steal cookies, send arbitrary requests, download malware, and deface the website using JavaScript code. The vulnerability was exploited by visiting a web server and clicking on a link that executed a malicious script.
1565615: Libcurl versions 7.82.0 to 7.83.0 were affected by a vulnerability that allowed arbitrary sites to set cookies that would get sent to a different and unrelated site or domain. This was due to a broken check that allowed cookies to be set for Top Level Domains (TLDs) if the host name was provided with a trailing dot. The vulnerability was fixed in version 7.83.1.
1565619: The curl URL parser allowed percent-encoded URL separators in the host name part of a URL, which could be used to circumvent filters and checks. This vulnerability was present in curl versions 7.80.0 to 7.83.0 and has been fixed in version 7.83.1.
1565622: Curl versions 7.82.0 to 7.83.0 were affected by a vulnerability that allowed HSTS bypass via trailing dot. This could trick curl into using HTTP instead of HTTPS, even when HTTPS was specified in the URL. The vulnerability was fixed in version 7.83.1.
1565623: Curl command versions 7.83.0 are vulnerable to a flaw that results in removal of a wrong file when combining `--no-clobber` and `--remove-on-error` if the target file name exists and an error occurs. This can lead to potential loss of integrity or availability. The flaw was fixed in version 7.83.1.
1565624: Libcurl, a widely used open-source library for transferring data over various protocols, was found to be vulnerable to a security flaw that allowed attackers to reuse previously created connections even when a TLS or SSH related option had been changed that should have prohibited reuse. The flaw was introduced in curl 7.16.1 and has been present in all versions up to and including 7.83.0. The vulnerability was assigned CVE-2022-27782 and has been patched in curl 7.83.1.
1566325: The Conduit feed.publish API allowed an attacker to spoof other users or make it look like they had access to a restricted object by manipulating the "authorPHID" and "objectPHID" parameters. This could result in false actions being attributed to users and cause confusion or suspicion. The API should have been restricted to prevent abuse.
1566758: A sensitive dashboard was exposed on a website, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive information. The vulnerability was discovered through Google Dorking and could be accessed without proper authentication. A CVE number was assigned to the vulnerability (CVE-2020-7130) and suggested mitigation includes protecting endpoints and collecting sensitive information on a local server.
1567186: A vulnerability was discovered in Reddit's "Sign in with Apple" feature that allowed attackers to hijack user accounts. The vulnerability was due to a response-type switch and leaking href to XSS on www.redditmedia.com. Attackers could steal OAuth codes and access-tokens using postMessage, allowing for a full account hijack of the account in Reddit. The vulnerability was mitigated by removing the fragment part when location is sent to www.redditmedia.com and restricting the redirect_uri of Apple-ID to something that does not load a domain that could run arbitrary javascript.
1569946: A vulnerability in Curl allowed for a denial-of-service attack due to a failure to limit the number of cookies that can be set by a single host/domain. This could lead to a situation where constructing the request towards a host would consume more memory than available, leading to an instant out-of-memory error. Any host in a given domain could target any other hosts in the same domain by using domain cookies. The attack worked from both HTTP and HTTPS and from unprivileged ports.
1570651: HTTP compression in Curl allowed for uncontrolled resource consumption, leading to application termination or system crashes. Attack vectors included sending repeated encodings in Transfer-Encoding or Content-Encoding headers, or sending many Set-Cookie headers with unique cookie names and large values.
1572591: A vulnerability was discovered in LinkedIn that allowed a lower privileged user to view the list of approved domains for email verification through the "Analyst" role by abusing the "GET /voyager/api/voyagerOrganizationDashEmailDomainMappings" endpoint. The vulnerability was due to insufficient access controls.
1573634: File permissions were not preserved in Curl when writing certain databases, including `CURLOPT_COOKIEJAR`, `CURLOPT_ALTSVC`, and `CURLOPT_HSTS`. As a result, files that were previously protected against read access by other users became readable by other users. This vulnerability could lead to the leak of sensitive information. Additionally, Curl would replace softlinks to the database with locally written databases, and specifying `"/dev/null"` as a file name could lead to system overwriting the special file and result in an inoperable system.
1574017: A vulnerability called Clickjacking was found on app.lemlist.com during security testing. The vulnerability allowed attackers to trick users into clicking on something different from what they perceived they were clicking on, potentially revealing confidential information or taking control of their computer. The server didn't return an X-Frame-Options header, which made the website at risk of a clickjacking attack. The vulnerability affected the web server and could have led to account takeover, account deletion, and password change.
1575912: Arbitrary headers could be injected and HTTP requests could be smuggled due to insufficient input validation in the `host_header` action parameter of the Origin Rules API. This vulnerability allowed bypassing security products and accessing internal origin servers. The issue was fixed by Cloudflare engineers and no customers were affected. It is recommended for Cloudflare Access customers to verify the Authorization JWT token before processing requests from the Cloudflare edge to prevent similar attempts.
1578400: An XSS vulnerability was discovered in GitLab 15.0.0 that allowed an attacker to execute JavaScript as an authenticated user when attempting to add or remove a contact for the new customer relations feature. The vulnerability was triggered by setting the contact's first name or last name to a malicious script.
1578574: An unauthenticated Mosquitto MQTT server was discovered on connect.acronis.com, allowing anyone to connect and read/write messages, potentially exposing client emails, IPs, and license keys. The recommendation was to enable authentication.
1579374: A vulnerability was discovered in the Brave browser where it did not follow proper redirection flow, causing an open redirect. This vulnerability affected Facebook's security and Brave's reputation, as users of the browser were directly affected. Other browsers were not affected.
1579645: The `v-safe-html` directive in GitLab was not safe enough as it did not remove the `data-disable-with` attribute from HTML tags, which allowed an attacker to bypass sanitization and execute arbitrary code on the client-side. This vulnerability could be exploited via job error messages that contained user-provided CI job names. An attacker could use this vulnerability to perform arbitrary actions on behalf of victims.
1579820: The Nextcloud Mail app was vulnerable to an ownership check bypass when updating or deleting attachments. An attacker could overwrite the local_message_id for an existing attachment or delete the given row, causing the attachment to be unavailable for the given message in the outbox. The impact was limited to the unavailability of the attachment for the affected message.
1580567: Exposed valid AWS, MySQL, Sendgrid, and other secrets were discovered, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive information.
1581059: An account takeover vulnerability was discovered in releases 3.18.5 and 3.0.5 of an unspecified software. An attacker with low privilege user access could obtain the admin reset token and set a new password for the admin user. The vulnerability was fixed in releases 3.18.6, 4.4.4, and 4.7.3.
1581240: An IDOR vulnerability was discovered in the user invite link in Taxjar, which could have allowed an attacker to take over a user's account without any user interaction. The vulnerability was caused by a leaked token in the delete invitation request feature and was resolved by using the invitation ID instead of the token to look up the user’s invite when deleting an invitation. Validation was added to ensure the ID belongs to the user’s organization.
1581528: A vulnerability existed in LinkedIn that allowed an attacker to report any unlisted job and access the name of the creator, name of the job, name of the company, and other details. The vulnerability was due to a lack of proper access controls and could be exploited by submitting a report using the draft, rejected, or under review job ID. The vulnerability has since been fixed.
1583680: Undici, when used with its ProxyAgent, did not use CONNECT or correctly verify the upstream server's HTTPS certificate. This allowed attackers on the network path between the client and the target server to perform trivial man-in-the-middle attacks, view or modify all request and response details, and expose all HTTPS traffic to plain-text HTTP. The vulnerability affected all use of HTTPS via an HTTP proxy with Undici or Node's global fetch.
1584409: The deprecated owners.query API in Phabricator did not check object view policy, allowing an attacker to view some information about an owner package they did not have permission to see, including name, description, owner PHIDs, repository PHIDs, and a path.
1584718: Sensitive information disclosure was possible in Shopify stores that had the Google Sales channel installed, even if the store was in password protection. Attackers could exploit this vulnerability by accessing a specific link with the product ID of the victim's store, which would reveal data-channel-id and data-user-email in the response.
1587374: The LinkedIn Campaign Manager API did not implement server-side authorization checks on a specific HTTP request, allowing an attacker to fetch the campaign wallet amount details and history of all the victim's account. This vulnerability could potentially lead to unauthorized access to sensitive financial information.
1588732: A vulnerability in GitLab allowed for a CSP-bypass XSS attack in the project settings page. The vulnerability was due to unsanitized deployment titles, which could be controlled by users and could contain arbitrary HTML content. This allowed for the execution of malicious scripts, despite the presence of a Content Security Policy (CSP) with 'strict-dynamic' value. The impact of the vulnerability was that attackers could perform arbitrary malicious requests on behalf of victims on HTTP client side.
1590071: A vulnerability in libcurl allowed a malicious attacker to inject arbitrary FTP server responses to GSSAPI protected FTP control connection and/or make the client consume unrelated heap memory as a FTP command response. The issue was caused by libcurl handling `gss_unwrap` `GSS_S_BAD_SIG` error incorrectly. The impact of this vulnerability was low, considering the rarity of Kerberos FTP and requirement of either man in the middle or victim connecting to malicious server.
1590237: An unauthenticated user could access private messages sent to teachers in Sensei LMS plugin versions up to 4.4.3 due to improper permissions set in one of its REST endpoints.
1591403: A self XSS vulnerability was discovered in the admin dashboard of https://linkpop.com. An attacker could execute arbitrary JavaScript code by inserting it into the URL input field and then clicking on the link that appears on the phone image. The impact of this vulnerability was limited to self XSS.
1591412: Pipeline job artifacts were exposed without IP restriction on the GitLab pages domain, allowing unauthenticated users outside the IP range to access them. This vulnerability was caused by a feature in GitLab that previews HTML artifacts safely, which is not restricted by the IP block. As a result, job IDs were leaked, making it possible for users to access the artifacts from any IP using the job ID.
1592587: A vulnerability was found in LinkedIn that allowed an attacker to delete the skill assessment result and gained badges of any user by replaying a vulnerable request using the victim's profile UUID and skill id. The UUID was publicly available in the page source of the victim's public profile.
1592596: An arbitrary private message sending vulnerability existed in Sensei LMS versions prior to 4.5.2. The vulnerability allowed any authenticated user to send messages to arbitrary private conversations via an IDOR attack, without ensuring that the sender was either the teacher or the original sender.
1593404: It was possible to bypass Cloudflare's 2FA when logging in with Apple ID authentication, allowing unauthorized access to Cloudflare accounts. The vulnerability was caused by a flaw in the authentication flow and could affect users whose Apple ID account was compromised or not linked to their Cloudflare profile. The issue was fixed by the engineering team.
1593413: An excessive lifetime was found in the OIDC JWT token generated by Sign in with Apple, allowing malicious actors to impersonate affected users on multiple devices without re-authentication. The issue was fixed by decreasing the token validity period.
1593913: A deserialization vulnerability was found in GitHub Enterprise Server that could have led to remote code execution on the SVNBridge. The vulnerability required an attacker to gain access via server-side request forgery (SSRF) to control the data being deserialized. The vulnerability affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to v3.6 and was fixed in versions 3.5.3, 3.4.6, 3.3.11, and 3.2.16.
1594627: A vulnerability in mod_proxy_ajp of Apache HTTP Server allowed an attacker to smuggle requests to the AJP server it forwards requests to, potentially resulting in information disclosure or remote code execution.
