1595006: An unauthenticated SSRF vulnerability was found in the "cerdic/csstidy" module included in the Nextcloud mail extension. The vulnerability allowed attackers to contact any remote server via HTTP, potentially leading to further attacks. The vulnerability was reported to the module developers for a fix.
1595281: A read-beyond-bounds vulnerability was found in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier versions, which could cause the server to crash or disclose information. The vulnerability was located in the ap_strcmp_match() function in server/util.c, which could be triggered by an attacker-provided input buffer of an extremely large size. While no code distributed with the server could be coerced into such a call, third-party modules or lua scripts that use ap_strcmp_match() may have been affected. The issue was fixed in version 2.4.54.
1595290: A vulnerability was found in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier that could allow an attacker to exfiltrate a controllable amount of heap data if the victim site runs a suitable LUA program. The bug is due to misuse of ap_get_brigade() and apr_bucket_read(). An attacker could repeatedly exfiltrate an attacker-determined amount of beyond-bounds heap data, which could contain anything that httpd previously had allocated from heap. The vulnerability has been assigned CVE-2022-30556, and Apache has released an update to address the issue.
1595296: A read-beyond-bounds vulnerability was found in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.53 and earlier on Windows when configured to process requests with the mod_isapi module. An attacker could potentially exploit this vulnerability to read beyond bounds and cause a crash. The issue was fixed in version 2.4.54.
1595299: A read beyond bounds vulnerability was found in Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.53 and earlier. The vulnerability could be exploited by an attacker to read unintended memory if the server reflects very large input using ap_rwrite() or ap_rputs(). The vulnerability has been patched in version 2.4.54.
1595905: A stored XSS vulnerability was found in the widget review form preview in the Judge.Me Shopify app. An attacker could add a payload to the success message, which would trigger when the form is previewed, and potentially execute malicious scripts. The vulnerability has been reported to the app's security team.
1596252: Apache HTTP Server versions 2.4.53 and earlier are vulnerable to a denial-of-service attack due to a lack of default limit on possible input size in the mod_lua r:parsebody function. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability by sending a malicious request to a Lua script that calls r:parsebody(0), causing the server to crash. The Apache HTTP Server project has released version 2.4.54 to address this vulnerability.
1596459: The Talk Android broadcast receiver was not protected by broadcastPermission, allowing a malicious app to communicate with the receiver without any permissions being checked. The impact of this vulnerability is uncertain but could potentially interfere with call starts and audio/bluetooth setup.
1596663: A hidden admin account could be created by an admin in an ads creating and managing application for Reddit, allowing them to perform administrative actions on the organization, such as removing or inviting users. The malicious account information could not be seen in the members section, and even the owner of the organization could not detect or remove the account. This was possible due to a flaw in the application's role management functionalities, which allowed a user with the same email to be invited to the same organization multiple times if assigned different roles.
1596673: The Nextcloud talk section was vulnerable to a lack of brute force protection while joining a password-protected video call. This allowed potential attackers to bypass the password protection.
1596918: Brute force protections in Nextcloud were not logging negative attempts and not throttling responses, leaving the system vulnerable to brute force attacks.
1599063: Undici.ProxyAgent was vulnerable to MITM attacks as it did not verify the remote server's certificate, allowing proxies to intercept all HTTPS traffic. This affected all usage of HTTPS via HTTP proxy using Undici.ProxyAgent with Undici or Node's global fetch, removing all HTTPS security from requests and allowing trivial MitM attacks by anyone on the network path. The issue was patched in Undici v5.5.1.
1599573: Rails::Html::SafeListSanitizer was vulnerable to an XSS attack in an environment that allowed the select and style tags. The vulnerability was caused by a difference between the nokogiri java implementation and the ruby implementation. The vulnerability impacted code only if allowed tags were being overridden. The issue was fixed in version 1.4.3. Users overriding the allowed tags by including both "select" and "style" were advised to upgrade or remove either select or style from the overridden allowed tags.
1600720: An HTML injection vulnerability was discovered in the registration process of Acronis Cyber Protect. An attacker could inject HTML tags into the "First Name" field, which would be executed when the victim receives an email from Acronis Cyber Protect. This could lead to potential harm to the victim and the company's reputation. The vulnerability was reported but not resolved.
1601140: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on panther.com, allowing an attacker to inject HTML and potentially execute JavaScript, leading to session theft. The vulnerability was caused by the application failing to sanitize user input.
1604606: The package was vulnerable to information exposure due to a failure to strip the Authorization header on HTTP downgrade. This vulnerability could have allowed an attacker to gain unauthorized access to sensitive information. The issue has been fixed in versions 7.4.4 and 6.5.7.
1605847: The Cloudflare WARP iOS mobile client had a vulnerability that allowed users to bypass the Lock WARP switch feature by enabling both "Disable for cellular networks" and "Disable for Wi-Fi networks" switches at once in the application settings. This caused the WARP client to disconnect and allowed users to bypass restrictions and policies enforced by the Zero Trust platform. The issue was fixed in version 6.14 of the iOS mobile client.
1605962: An internal email of a Shopify store was disclosed through the Shopify Data Exporter app. The email was exposed through a request that could be accessed by anyone, revealing the email address in the response. This vulnerability allowed unauthorized access to sensitive information.
1606039: Libcurl, a widely used client-side URL transfer library, was found to have a vulnerability that could allow a malicious server to cause a never-ending busy-loop when trying to retrieve TLS server certificate chain information using the CURLOPT_CERTINFO option. The flaw was introduced in curl 7.34.0 and was fixed in curl 7.83.1. Users are advised to upgrade to the latest version or apply the patch to their local version.
1606068: Multiple hosts were found to be vulnerable to Cisco ASA XSS CVE-2020-3580, which targeted the saml service within the VPN. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to steal user cookies or redirect users to malicious websites. A patch was released to mitigate this vulnerability.
1606961: A vulnerability was found in Nextcloud's password generator, where in rare cases, a password generated by the server may not be fully validated by HIBPValidator after the shuffle function str_shuffle() is called, resulting in weak passwords.
1607429: A broken link in the Twitter icon on the website runpanther.io allowed anyone to create a Twitter account with the same username, potentially leading to account impersonation and scams.
1607601: The Nextcloud/logger NPM package was vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) due to the sub-patterns [[\\]()#;?]* and (?:;[-a-zA-Z\\d\\/#&.:=?%@~_]*)*. Attackers could exploit this vulnerability to make the system inaccessible to legitimate users. The vulnerability was fixed in versions 4.1.1, 5.0.1, and 6.0.1.
1608039: The Nextcloud application was vulnerable to SSRF attacks due to a lack of metadata checks in the `preventLocalAddress` function. This allowed an attacker to bypass the filter and access metadata from cloud providers like Google Cloud and Alibaba. A security advisory was issued for this vulnerability.
1609965: Arbitrary command execution was possible on GitLab servers via the `DecompressedArchiveSizeValidator` and Project BulkImports (behind feature flag). An attacker could exploit this vulnerability if the `bulk_import_projects` feature was enabled. This vulnerability has been patched.
1613714: A vulnerability was disclosed that allowed access to non-revoked API key information through the Stripo_report() function. This has since been fixed.
1613943: A vulnerability was discovered in cURL that allowed an attacker to store cookies with control characters in the cookie store, causing cURL to generate large requests that would result in a 400 error from the server, preventing further interaction with the server. This could be exploited by an attacker to prevent a user or application from interacting with a particular HTTP server with the same cookie store.
1614328: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-32205) in curl versions 7.71.0 to 7.83.1 allowed a malicious server to cause a denial of service by serving excessive amounts of Set-Cookie headers in a HTTP response, causing subsequent HTTP requests to become larger than the threshold that curl uses internally to avoid sending large requests. The vulnerability was fixed in curl version 7.84.0.
1614330: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-32206) existed in curl versions 7.57.0 to 7.83.1 that allowed a malicious server to insert an unlimited number of compression steps, resulting in a "malloc bomb" and denial of service. The vulnerability was fixed in curl version 7.84.0 by capping the number of accepted "chained" algorithms to 5. Automatic decompression of content needed to be enabled per transfer for the vulnerability to be exploited.
1614331: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-32207) in curl versions 7.69.0 to 7.83.1 allowed for unpreserved file permissions when saving cookies, alt-svc, and hsts data to local files, potentially leaving the updated file accessible to more users than intended. The issue was fixed in curl version 7.84.0.
1614332: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-32208) existed in curl versions 7.16.4 to 7.83.1 when performing FTP transfers secured by krb5, which could allow a Man-In-The-Middle attack to go unnoticed and even inject data to the client due to incorrect handling of message verification failures. The flaw was fixed in curl version 7.84.0. It is recommended to upgrade to the fixed version or apply the patch.
1615790: An expired password reset link on the Altaro VM Backup website could still be used to reset the password, as the link remained linked with the "__VIEWSTATE" parameter on the server side. This allowed an attacker with access to the victim's inbox to use any expired link to change the user's password. The vulnerability was reported to the vendor.
1619604: A vulnerability existed in versions of `cmark-gfm` prior to `0.29.0.gfm.6` that allowed unauthenticated users to cause denial of service attacks via the markdown API due to a polynomial time complexity issue in the autolink extension. The vulnerability has been patched, and users are advised to upgrade or disable the autolink extension.
1620170: A vulnerability in Mattermost server allowed an attacker to crash the server by sending a specially crafted GIF with maximum dimensions through the upload API, causing the server to consume more than 4GB of RAM. The vulnerability was triggered by the `gif.DecodeAll` function being called without any call to `preprocessImage`.
1620247: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was discovered in the first name and last name fields of the registration page of a website. An attacker could execute malicious JavaScript payloads, potentially compromising user data. The vulnerability was mitigated by filtering input on arrival, encoding data on output, and implementing a content security policy.
1622449: In June 2022, a former employee of HackerOne improperly accessed vulnerability data of customers to re-submit duplicate vulnerabilities to those same customers for personal gain. The incident was discovered after a customer reported receiving a threatening communication outside the HackerOne platform about a vulnerability disclosure. The employee was terminated, and steps were taken to contain the insider's access. The incident prompted HackerOne to implement additional improvements to their logging, detection and response, hiring screening, data isolation, and red team tabletops.
1623685: A SSRF vulnerability was discovered that allowed remote access to AWS metadata through the use of the parameter "?url=". The vulnerability could be exploited to tunnel into internal networks and access sensitive internal data. The suggested mitigation actions include sanitizing user-supplied input in the parameter and blocking access to internal networks.
1624137: A vulnerability in the Java package log4j, identified as CVE-2021-44228, allowed for remote code execution (RCE) on affected systems. An attacker could exploit the vulnerability by sending a specially crafted request to the system, which would trigger the execution of arbitrary code. Mitigation and remediation actions are available to address the vulnerability.
1624140: The domain was vulnerable to Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks via the URL parameter, allowing an attacker to fetch AWS metadata by abusing the SSRF at a specific URL. This could result in unauthorized access to data within the organization. The vulnerability was exploited to expose AWS metadata and credentials.
1624152: Private repositories on a GitLab instance were insecure and accessible to unauthenticated users, allowing for information disclosure and potential access to source code. The vulnerability was caused by a misconfiguration of access controls.
1625652: A delimiter injection vulnerability was discovered in the `core.exportVariable` function of the GitHub Actions ToolKit. Attackers could exploit this vulnerability to modify the path or other environment variables by injecting a specific delimiter into untrusted values written to the `GITHUB_ENV` file. The vulnerability was fixed in `@actions/core v1.9.1`.
1626198: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered on the endpoint `/olc/set/m101/leasib.php` of a website, allowing a remote attacker to gain access to the database by exploiting the vulnerable parameters `scn`, `SUBJECT`, and `COURSEID`. Thirteen databases were found to be available.
1626210: A local file read vulnerability was discovered in a website's endpoint that allowed an attacker to read any local files by exploiting the vulnerable `filePathDownload` path. The vulnerability was caused by insufficient protection in place, which was bypassed by the attacker. The impact of the vulnerability was that an attacker could potentially access sensitive information.
1626226: An unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability was discovered at a certain organization's website. Due to non-filter and non-escape input at the API, an attacker could inject malicious payload after a single quote (') to exploit and extract the database. The vulnerability allowed the attacker to extract sensitive information from the server.
1626281: A password reset token was found to be leaked to third-party sites, potentially allowing malicious users to reset the passwords of victims.
1626356: A vulnerability was discovered that allowed an attacker to perform a cross-site request forgery attack on a website's registration page, leading to the takeover of user accounts. The attack was possible due to the lack of anti-CSRF tokens and the website's practice of sending passwords to unverified email addresses.
1626962: Reflected XSS was discovered on a contact form on a website, allowing for possible insertion of `"` characters and execution of JavaScript code. This could potentially allow an attacker to perform actions within the application, view or modify information, and initiate interactions with other users.
1627159: A vulnerability was found in the multipart parsing component of Rack, which could allow a denial of service attack. The vulnerability affected versions 1.2 and above, and was fixed in versions 2.0.9.1, 2.1.4.1, and 2.2.3.1. The vulnerability could be triggered by carefully crafted multipart POST requests, causing the parser to take much longer than expected. This could lead to a possible denial of service attack.
1627616: The vulnerability allowed for RXSS on a system host due to the lack of filtering on the "WhatSubmitted" parameter, which allowed for the execution of JS code. This could have resulted in the attacker performing any action within the application that the user can perform, viewing any information that the user is able to view, modifying any information that the user is able to modify, and initiating interactions with other application users. The suggested mitigation actions include filtering input on arrival, encoding data on output, using appropriate response headers, and implementing Content Security Policy.
1627961: An endpoint in ████████ was vulnerable to account takeover. An attacker could change the email and user ID of their own account to that of a victim's account, allowing them to take over the victim's account.
1627962: An unauthenticated person could obtain personally identifiable information (PII) from verified or requested-to-be-verified profiles on a certain endpoint of a website. The endpoint could be accessed by unauthenticated users, and switching to the verified/requested-to-be-verified version of a profile would reveal the author's email in addition to their ID, UUID, and name.
1627970: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered in the `/olc/setlogin.php` endpoint of a website. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to inject malicious SQL code through the `username` and `password` parameters, potentially leading to unauthorized access to the database. The vulnerability was exploited using time-based techniques and SQLmap. The impact of the vulnerability was the ability for an attacker to access the database.
1627974: An IDOR vulnerability was found on a certain endpoint of a website, allowing an attacker to brute-force and delete companies by changing the ID parameter in the delete request. This could lead to the deletion of all companies on the website.
1627995: A SQL injection vulnerability was discovered in the `/olc/███comments/comment_post.php` endpoint of a website, allowing an attacker to extract sensitive information from the database. The vulnerable parameter was `staff_student`.
1628012: An IDOR vulnerability allowed a user with member permission in an organization to create, view, and delete private API keys. An attacker could invite themselves as a member, access the API key endpoint, and perform unauthorized actions on the API keys.
1628102: A full read SSRF vulnerability was found in a website, allowing attackers to hit the AWS Metadata endpoint and potentially dump AWS keys and reach internal hosts. The vulnerability was exploited by entering a specific input for LRS URL and creating a new LRS configuration. The attacker could then download a log file containing the response from the AWS metadata endpoint.
1628209: A vulnerability was discovered in the Functional Administrative Support Tool (FAST) v1.0 that allowed an attacker to inject a malicious JavaScript payload during the PDF form creation process, which was then executed by the checklist application server. This could be used to steal sensitive information from an AWS instance.
1630336: A bypass vulnerability was discovered in Node.js HTTP parser (CVE-2022-32213) that allowed HTTP request smuggling attacks. The vulnerability was caused by the parser incorrectly folding headers and forwarding an invalid `Transfer-Encoding` header to the downstream server. This could lead to HTTP request smuggling attacks.
1630667: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-32215) was found in the llhttp parser in the http module of Node.js, which could lead to HTTP Request Smuggling (HRS) due to incorrect parsing of multi-line Transfer-Encoding headers. This vulnerability impacted all versions of the 18.x, 16.x, and 14.x releases lines. The issue was fixed in llhttp v6.0.7 and llhttp v2.1.5, which were updated inside Node.js.
1630668: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-32213) was found in the llhttp parser in the http module of Node.js, which could allow for HTTP Request Smuggling (HRS) due to flawed parsing and validation of Transfer-Encoding headers. This vulnerability impacted all versions of the 18.x, 16.x, and 14.x release lines. The issue was fixed in llhttp v6.0.7 and llhttp v2.1.5, which were updated inside Node.js.
1630669: HTTP Request Smuggling vulnerability (CVE-2022-32214) was discovered in Node.js versions 18.x, 16.x, and 14.x releases lines. The vulnerability was caused by the llhttp parser in the http module, which did not strictly use the CRLF sequence to delimit HTTP requests, leading to potential HTTP Request Smuggling attacks. The vulnerability was fixed in llhttp v6.0.7 and llhttp v2.1.5, which were updated inside Node.js.
1631350: Multiple off-by-slash misconfigurations were found in the configuration files for Nginx in the nodejs/build repository, which were deployed on nodejs.org and iojs.org. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to access unexpected directories and view sensitive files in the `/home/dist` directory.
1631364: A log4j vulnerability was found in the application, which could result in remote code execution if untrusted or user-controlled data is logged. The vulnerability affected the system host(s) and could be exploited by sending a POST request to a specific endpoint. Mitigation and remediation actions were suggested.
1631370: A Solr log4j vulnerability was found that allowed for remote code execution by logging untrusted or user-controlled data. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a GET request to a specific path and changing the interact server. Mitigation and remediation actions are suggested.
1631447: A stored XSS vulnerability was found in the login page of a website. The vulnerability was caused by the exposure of the "edit" GET parameter, which revealed a hidden markdown editor. An attacker could input and execute their own JavaScript code that would execute on everyone who accessed the login page every time. The vulnerability could also be used to upload images and deface the website. The only way to remove the XSS payload was to access the markdown editor and remove it.
1632921: A vulnerability existed in the --inspect option of Node.js due to an insufficient fix of a previous vulnerability. This allowed an attacker-controlled DNS server to bypass DNS rebinding protection by resolving hosts in the .local domain, potentially leading to remote code execution. The vulnerability was caused by allowing the use of the 0.0.0.0 IP address, which is a reserved address range, and could be exploited by an attacker with access to a compromised DNS server or the ability to spoof its responses.
1633231: A vulnerability in the WARP mobile client on iOS allowed users to delete VPN profiles despite the Lock WARP switch being enabled, potentially bypassing policies and restrictions enforced by the Zero Trust platform. The issue was fixed in version 6.15 of the mobile client.
1634105: An open redirect vulnerability was found on a website, allowing an attacker to redirect users to a malicious site. The vulnerable parameter was "u". No CVE numbers were assigned, and mitigation/remediation actions were not suggested.
1635321: Unsanitized input from an argument can flow into java.io.FileOutputStream, resulting in a Path Traversal vulnerability that allows an attacker to write to arbitrary files. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized access and manipulation of sensitive files on the server.
1635854: A remote denial of service vulnerability was discovered in HyperLedger Fabric. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to crash as many peers as they want. The vulnerability was caused by an invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference.
1636345: The application was found to be vulnerable to reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, which could allow an attacker to run malicious scripts on a victim's browser. This could lead to cookie stealing, arbitrary requests, malware downloads, and defacement of the website. A proof-of-concept attack was provided. No mitigation or remediation actions were suggested.
1636552: The email verification process in Khan Academy's signup allowed users to add and verify any email as a guardian's email, bypassing the verification process. This vulnerability could potentially allow attackers to gain unauthorized access to accounts.
1636566: Node.js versions prior to 16.16.0 and 14.20.0 were vulnerable to DLL hijacking on Windows. Attackers could exploit this vulnerability to escalate privileges and establish persistence in a target environment. The vulnerability could also provide another way to embed malicious code into packages. The vulnerability was fixed in Node.js 16.16.0 and 14.20.0 versions.
1637621: A vulnerability was discovered in GitHub Actions Runner versions prior to 2.296.2, 2.293.1, 2.289.4, 2.285.2, and 2.283.4 that allowed an input to escape the environment variable and modify the docker command invocation directly, potentially leading to command injection. The vulnerability affected jobs that use container actions, job containers, or service containers alongside untrusted user inputs in environment variables. The issue has been patched, and users are advised to upgrade their runner versions or remove any container actions, job containers, or service containers from their jobs as a workaround.
1641088: A vulnerability existed in Nextcloud Talk that allowed an attacker to view the last video frame of any participant who had disabled video but had a camera selected. This was due to the last frame of the video being sent even after the video was disabled in a call. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to access the last video frame of any participant.
1641148: A directory traversal vulnerability was found in a Windows Server at a certain host, allowing an attacker to read sensitive files on the server by manipulating the "path" parameter in an HTTP GET request. Input validation for the "path" parameter is recommended as a mitigation measure.
1643962: A file disclosure vulnerability was discovered in the influxdb.quality.gitlab.net domain, allowing attackers to read arbitrary files on the server without authentication. This could include sensitive data, credentials, and application code.
1644436: An IDOR vulnerability was discovered in the Exness PA stats API endpoint, allowing an attacker to view the equity or net profit of any MT account by manipulating the `accounts` parameter. The vulnerability was exploitable through several endpoints responsible for fetching the stats performance chart.
1646248: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on videostore.mtnonline.com, allowing an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript code on the victim's browser.
1646554: An unclaimed CNAME record was found on the subdomain support.invisionpower.com, which made it vulnerable to subdomain takeover. An attacker could have exploited this vulnerability by registering the expired subdomain and setting up a phishing page that mimics the company's main support website. This could have led to various malicious activities such as malware distribution, phishing, XSS, authentication bypass, and more.
1647287: A vulnerability in Electron allowed a compromised child renderer process to obtain IPC access without nodeIntegrationInSubFrames being enabled, potentially leading to Remote Code Execution if there are sensitive IPC handlers on the main process. The vulnerability was patched in versions 15.5.5, 16.2.6, 17.2.0, and 18.0.0-beta.6. A workaround is to ensure that all IPC message handlers appropriately validate senderFrame.
1650273: There was an off-by-slash vulnerability in the configuration files for Nginx in nodejs.org and iojs.org, which allowed attackers to access unexpected directories and potentially sensitive files in the /home/dist directory. The vulnerability was fixed by correcting the misconfiguration in the Nginx files.
1652042: A possible code injection vulnerability was found in the Active Storage module of Rails, affecting versions >= 5.2.0 and impacting applications that use Active Storage with the image_processing processing in addition to the mini_magick back end for image_processing. The vulnerability could allow an attacker to achieve RCE by exploiting untrusted arbitrary input in the transformation method or its arguments. Fixed versions are available, and workarounds include implementing a strict allow-list on accepted transformation methods or arguments and a strict image magick security policy.
1652046: A stored cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability was found in Dovetale, an influencer platform from Shopify. An attacker could inject malicious code into the application form, which would be stored and executed when an admin approves the application. This could lead to the execution of JavaScript code, data exfiltration, defacement of the site, and phishing attacks.
1652903: Clear-text connection credentials were logged in the Nextcloud log when exceptions were thrown in the context of the SharePoint app, potentially exposing them to attackers who gain access to the log.
1654145: An Amazon S3 bucket belonging to GoCD was misconfigured, allowing any unauthenticated user to access and download sensitive files stored in the bucket. The vulnerability was caused by improper configuration of the S3 bucket, which allowed unrestricted access to its contents.
1654310: A vulnerability in Rails::Html::SafeListSanitizer allowed an attacker to bypass filtering and perform an XSS attack. The incomplete fix for the vulnerability only considered one way of passing the list of allowed tags to the sanitizer, leaving the other way vulnerable. Updating to rails-html-sanitizer 1.4.3 did not fix the issue in certain configurations. A patch has been released to complete the fix.
1656380: A vulnerability was discovered in Reddit Talk promotion offers, where the offerIds created for promoting a user to a speaker/host did not expire. This allowed users to accept the offerIds even after being demoted back to a listener, effectively allowing them to regain their promoted role and potentially causing interruptions to the Reddit Talk.
1656627: Rails::Html::SafeListSanitizer was vulnerable to XSS attacks when certain combinations of tags were allowed in the allow list. Specifically, allowing `svg` and `style` or `math` and `style` tags in the allow list could lead to XSS attacks. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to execute arbitrary code in the context of a victim's browser. A patch has been released to address this vulnerability.
1658418: An IDOR vulnerability allowed attackers to access the mod logs of any public or restricted subreddit by changing the parameter "subredditName" in a request to gql.reddit.com. The vulnerability did not check if the user was a moderator of the subreddit or not. This could result in the exposure of confidential information.
1661113: An IDOR vulnerability was discovered that allowed an attacker to modify the links of any user on Reddit. By replicating a request and replacing it with their own authentication headers, an attacker could obtain the links of any user profile with the "id" of each link. The attacker could then modify the links by putting in the request body, in the "id" parameter, the previously saved id, and changing the name and link. The impact of this vulnerability is that an attacker could modify the name and content of any user's social links.
1662194: Sensitive data, specifically the secret API key, was being logged in clear text in the Omise Python repository. This could have resulted in the exposure of the key in recorded demonstrations, copied logs, and other unusual places. The suggested remediation was to either log only a partial part of the key or remove the logging entirely.
1662474: An information disclosure vulnerability was found in the Spring Boot Actuator v3. By accessing certain endpoints, an attacker could obtain sensitive information about the application, such as a list of all Spring beans, internal paths, ports, version numbers, and more. The vulnerability was mitigated by disabling the endpoints or configuring their enablement.
1663299: The HackerOne internal backend interface had a SQL injection vulnerability that allowed an attacker to escape the transaction wrapped around the `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` query, leading to arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability was due to the ability to interpolate the `raw_sql` variable. The attacker could inject a payload into the `user_versions` table and use the `reify` method to execute arbitrary ruby code. The impact was the execution of arbitrary ruby code.
1663363: A vulnerability was found in WordPress that allowed anyone to access the usernames and some information of all the users/authors through the REST API endpoint /wp-json/wp/v2/users/. This could potentially lead to brute force attacks on the disclosed usernames.
1663788: Undici, a Node.js HTTP client library, was vulnerable to SSRF (Server-side Request Forgery) due to improper processing of user input in the `pathname` option of the `undici.request` function. This vulnerability could allow an attacker to send arbitrary requests to internal systems or external systems accessible to the server. The issue was fixed in version 5.8.2.
1664019: A CRLF injection vulnerability existed in the 'content-type' header of the Node.js 'undici' library, affecting versions up to 5.8.1. This vulnerability allowed attackers to inject additional HTTP requests into a single request API call. The issue was resolved in version 5.8.2.
1665156: A vulnerability was discovered in the `llhttp` parser in the `http` module in Node.js versions 16.16.0 and 18.7.0, which allowed for HTTP Request Smuggling (HRS) due to incorrect parsing of multi-line Transfer-Encoding headers. This was due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2022-32215. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to bypass security layers, steal credentials, and perform other malicious actions.
1667974: Apache HTTP Server 2.4.52 and earlier versions were vulnerable to an HTTP request smuggling attack due to a failure to close inbound connections when errors were encountered discarding the request body. The vulnerability was fixed in version 2.4.53, released on March 14, 2022.
1668028: The Nextcloud Desktop Client application was vulnerable to a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack due to improper neutralization of file names. An attacker could inject arbitrary HTML into the application by renaming a file with HTML tags, causing the application to display the file name as HTML.
1671140: A command injection vulnerability (RCE) existed in the example DAG script of Apache Airflow Docker Provider <3.0, allowing an authenticated attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the Airflow worker host. The vulnerability was caused by externally controllable parameters rendered through a jinja2 template and executed as a bash script. The vulnerability was fixed in apache-airflow-providers-docker 3.0.0 or above.
1672388: A vulnerability was discovered in GitLab that allowed for remote code execution via a specially crafted response from GitHub. The vulnerability was due to the use of Sawyer::Resource to represent results, which allowed for the injection of additional Redis commands. This could be exploited to escalate to execute any Bash command. The vulnerability was tested on GitLab.com and was found to be exploitable.
1672459: A cross-site scripting vulnerability was discovered on api.collabs.shopify.com, which allowed for the execution of JavaScript code in the victim's browser and potential exfiltration of confidential data. The vulnerability was discovered through the registration process on the Shopify collabs platform.
1675014: User profiles of disabled users remained accessible on DOMAIN/u/USERID, exposing their personal information without their control or consent.
1675191: HTTP Request Smuggling vulnerability was discovered in the `llhttp` parser of the `http` module in Node v18.7.0. The vulnerability was caused by incorrect handling of header fields that are not terminated with CLRF, which could result in HTTP Request Smuggling. This could lead to access control bypass and other issues.
1679624: Arbitrary Redis commands could be executed on GitLab servers via a remote command execution vulnerability when importing a GitHub repository. The vulnerability was caused by the `Sawyer` library, which allowed an attacker to override built-in methods, and the Redis gem, which used `to_s` and `bytesize` to generate the RESP command. An attacker could inject arbitrary Redis commands by passing a `Sawyer::Resource` object with a controllable hash to Redis. This could be combined with a call to `Marshal.load` to execute a deserialization gadget and gain remote code execution. The vulnerability was patched in GitLab 15.3.1-ee.
1679969: A vulnerability was found in the host header of a domain, allowing an attacker to manipulate the header and cause unexpected behavior in the web application. This could lead to various attacks, including web cache poisoning, password reset poisoning, cross-site scripting, access to internal hosts, and phishing attacks. The suggested mitigation and remediation actions include validating the host header, using a whitelist of domains, and configuring a parameter for the Rule Execution Server.
1680241: An attacker could exploit a vulnerability in Mattermost to launch a denial-of-service (DoS) attack on the application server. The vulnerability was due to the lack of size check or validation in the automatic response message, which allowed an attacker to set an almost unlimited number of characters as the response value. By sending a large number of requests with a payload of up to 50MB, the server would consume an abnormal quantity of computing resources, ultimately leading to a server crash and making the application unavailable to all its users.
1680818: An Insecure Direct Object Reference vulnerability was found in certain Rockstar Official Crews on the Social Club website, allowing attackers to alter certain Crew settings via direct POST requests sent to the appropriate endpoints. The vulnerability was caused by users in the eCola Official and Sprunk Official Crews being mistakenly set to Commissioner-level rank as the default pattern. The issue has been resolved by updating the Crews so that users no longer have max-rank permissions and resetting the Crew settings to their intended values.
1681208: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found in ServiceNow through San Diego Patch 4b and Patch 6, allowing attackers to steal victims' cookies and perform malicious activities. The vulnerability was triggered by a crafted URL in the logout functionality.
1685822: Arbitrary local git repositories could be imported into GitLab via the `RepositoryPipeline` when importing a project via the BulkImports. This allowed an attacker to clone any repository on GitLab with just the project ID. The vulnerability was due to the `RepositoryPipeline` allowing arbitrary URL protocols to be passed to `project.repository.fetch_as_mirror(url)`.
1685970: The vulnerability discovered at https://app.taxjar.com/ was an improper access control issue that could have allowed for mass accounts takeover. It was caused by not correctly validating the reset password token, which was resolved by relying on the user fetched from the reset password token instead of the account ID provided in the URL.
1685979: An attacker could create a playbook with a large value for the `run_summary_template` attribute, which doesn't have any size check or validation. This could cause the server to consume an abnormal amount of computing resources and ultimately crash, leading to a denial of service attack. The attack is worsened by the fact that the user who created the playbook run cannot finish its execution via the Web Portal after the application is restarted.
1686935: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-35252) was found in curl versions 4.9 to 7.84.0 that allowed cookies with control codes to be accepted, which could cause HTTP(S) servers to return a 400 response, resulting in a denial of service. The issue was fixed in curl version 7.85.0.
1687005: Sensitive information such as OIDC client secrets and tokens were transferred in an unencrypted manner over plain HTTP without TLS in the OpenID Connect User Backend of Nextcloud, allowing an attacker to intercept and read the information.
1687410: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) was possible in the OpenID Connect User Backend module of Nextcloud due to insufficient encoding or filtering of the `authorization_endpoint` parameter. The vulnerability was limited to Safari browsers and was further mitigated by a restrictive Content-Security-Policy applied on the affected endpoint.
1688199: A vulnerability in Nextcloud allowed registered users to generate a massive database load by sharing folders with circles, resulting in resource exhaustion for logged-in users. This could lead to a slow down of the system and cause stress on servers. The vulnerability was present in Nextcloud version 23.0.8.
1690000: A vulnerability existed in WebCrypto keygen in Node.js due to the lack of checking the return value of `EntropySource()`, which sometimes fails, and the random data returned by `EntropySource()` may not be cryptographically strong and therefore not suitable as keying material. This could result in weak random data being written to the output buffer, which could be predicted or manipulated by an external attacker, leading to a complete breakdown of confidentiality and integrity.
1690044: An IDOR vulnerability was discovered on a domain, allowing an attacker to steal users' information via the VendorId parameter and potentially use it for phishing or account takeovers. The vulnerability was reported to the affected organization.
1690093: An insecure umask was configured for numerous Apache Airflow components when running with the `--daemon` flag prior to version 2.3.4, which could result in a race condition giving world-writable files in the Airflow home directory and allowing local users to expose arbitrary file contents via the webserver.
1690427: An improper privilege management vulnerability was found in GitHub Enterprise Server that allowed users with improper privileges to create or delete pages via the API. The vulnerability required the attacker to have write permissions and affected all versions of GitHub Enterprise Server prior to 3.7. It was fixed in versions 3.2.20, 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.7, and 3.6.3. The vulnerability was reported via the GitHub Bug Bounty program.
1690548: An authentication bypass vulnerability was discovered on a subdomain of the U.S Air Force domain. An attacker was able to bypass authentication and access sensitive data and functionality, potentially exposing additional attack surface for further exploits. The vulnerability allowed for sensitive information disclosure.
1690951: A subdomain takeover vulnerability was discovered at course.oberlo.com, which allowed an attacker to take control of the subdomain using kajabi services. The impact of subdomain takeovers can be severe, including malware, phishing, XSS, authentication bypass, open redirects, and true access. The suggested fix was to clear the subdomain DNS.
1691501: A blind SSRF vulnerability was discovered on a web application that allowed attackers to make the server connect to internal-only services or arbitrary external systems, potentially leaking sensitive data or performing unauthorized actions. The vulnerability was found in the image upload URL downloader feature, which allowed attackers to upload a payload and observe HTTP and DNS interactions. The vulnerability was exploited by using a payload in the URL downloader and polling it in a Burp Collaborator client. The suggested mitigation was to create a whitelist of domains in DNS and to enable authentication on all services.
1695454: An IDOR vulnerability was discovered in Pressable's API applications, allowing an attacker to view any API token and potentially take over the victim's account. By changing the application ID parameter in a POST request and removing all other parameters except the authenticity token, the attacker could access the victim's API credentials, including the client ID and client secret. The impact was critical as the attacker could access many things via the API, including the collaborator endpoint.
1695472: A vulnerability was discovered in the DOS validator nodes of a blockchain, which allowed an attacker to send a large number of read requests to each node, resulting in a denial-of-service attack that made the network unreachable for other clients. The attack did not cause damage to the blockchain, but it prevented the network from being used for its intended purpose until the attack was concluded.
1695596: During Node.js startup, OpenSSL reads the `openssl.cnf` file to configure itself. In Node.js 18 and later versions, on macOS, OpenSSL attempts to read the `openssl.cnf` file from `/home/iojs/build/ws/out/Release/obj.target/deps/openssl/openssl.cnf`, which does not exist. This could allow an attacker with access to a shared macOS host with a self-chosen username to affect the OpenSSF configuration of other users. The vulnerability was fixed by updating the OpenSSL configuration path in the Node.js build.
1698006: An IDOR vulnerability was discovered in mtnmobad.mtnbusiness.com.ng that allowed an attacker to change every user's account information by modifying the ID and email in the request payload.
1699740: A vulnerability in Nextcloudcmd allowed it to incorrectly trust bad TLS certificates, potentially exposing users to man-in-the-middle attacks. The issue was caused by the program disregarding certificate validation failures and proceeding with the sync anyway. The vulnerability was fixed in version 3.3.1 of the Nextcloud Desktop Client.
1699762: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found in the `utm_source` parameter of `www.shopify.com/markets`. An attacker could execute arbitrary code in the victim's browser by tricking them into clicking on a specially crafted link. The vulnerability has been reported to the affected company.
1700276: The R2 Custom Domain feature in Cloudflare allowed an attacker to take over any subdomain of r2.dev without being verified. This was due to a lack of domain validation when adding a domain to the account. The vulnerability was fixed by implementing a control to verify that the R2 Custom Domain added has been verified and belongs to the same Cloudflare account. No evidence of abuse by anyone other than the researcher was found, and there was no impact to any customer.
1700896: The Nagios dashboard in omon1.fpki.gov and 3.220.248.203 was accessible using default credentials, allowing an attacker to gain full control over the panel.
1703733: Sensitive information, including the admin username and password, was exposed on a subdomain of MTN Online. The password was stored in MD5 format, which was easily decrypted by the researcher who discovered the vulnerability. This could have allowed an attacker to access client information and potentially cause harm.
1704017: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-32221) existed in libcurl that caused an HTTP PUT to occur when the user intended for an HTTP POST to occur, potentially leading to information disclosure and use-after-free issues. An attacker could potentially inject data, either from stdin or from an unintended buffer, and sensitive information could be exposed to an unintended recipient. The vulnerability has been fixed.
1705717: A vulnerability in the `indy-node` code allowed an unauthenticated attacker to remotely execute code on every node in the network. The issue was related to the `POOL_UPGRADE` request handler, which handled an undocumented field called `package` that could contain the name of the package to be upgraded. If this field was not empty, it was passed as is to a system command without any sanitization, allowing an attacker to inject arbitrary commands. This could lead to remote code execution and potentially take control of the node and the entire network.
1706248: A vulnerability in Nextcloud Talk allowed guests to continue receiving video streams from a call after being removed from a conversation, potentially allowing an attacker to spy on calls in a public conversation. The issue occurred when the High Performance Backend was used.
1707977: The Nextcloud Desktop Client application was vulnerable to cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks via user status and information. Attackers could inject arbitrary HTML into the application by setting the Full Name and Status Message of their user profile on the Nextcloud server.
1710652: A vulnerability in Node.js allowed DNS rebinding attacks in --inspect via an invalid octal IP address. This allowed attackers to execute arbitrary code by bypassing the DNS rebinding protection.
1711847: The Nextcloud Desktop Client application was vulnerable to a cross-site scripting (XSS) attack in the call notification popup due to improper neutralization of the name of a group conversation. An attacker could inject arbitrary HTML into the application.
1711890: The subdomain 'de-headless.staging.gymshark.com' was vulnerable to subdomain takeover due to an unclaimed Shopify site. An attacker could have claimed the subdomain and served malicious content, including phishing campaigns, without being detected. The vulnerability was remediated by removing the CNAME record for Shopify on the subdomain.
1712329: The affected versions of Moment.js, a JavaScript date library, were vulnerable to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS) attacks via the preprocessRFC2822() function in from-string.js, when processing a very long crafted string (over 10k characters). This could cause a Denial of Service (DoS) attack, making the system inaccessible to its original and legitimate users. The vulnerability had a CVSS score of 3.1/10 and users who passed user-provided strings without sanity length checks to Moment.js constructor were vulnerable to (Re)DoS attacks.
1714563: The Jolokia 1.3.5 version was vulnerable to a reflected XSS vulnerability (CVE-2018-1000129). The vulnerability was discovered during reconnaissance on a website.
1715536: A vulnerability in Fastify versions before 4.6.1 allowed an attacker to crash the server by sending a specially crafted Content-Type header. The issue was caused by a lack of proper validation of the requested content-type parser, which could result in the application crashing when the parser function was called. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause a denial of service attack.
1717626: A subdomain takeover vulnerability was discovered on http://www.codefi.consensys.net/, which occurs when an attacker gains control over a subdomain of a target domain that has a canonical name (CNAME) in the Domain Name System (DNS), but no host is providing content for it. The attacker can take over that subdomain by providing their own virtual host and then hosting their own content for it, potentially enabling them to capture protected information or send malicious content to unsuspecting users.
1718371: A subdomain takeover vulnerability was discovered at http://test.www.midigator.com, where the subdomain pointed to an AWS S3 bucket that no longer existed, allowing an attacker to take control of the bucket and serve their own content on it. The vulnerability was remediated by removing the CNAME entry for the subdomain.
1718574: A malicious admin was able to permanently disable an owner (admin) to access their account.
1719719: Mail.acronis.com was vulnerable to a zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2022-41040, which could have allowed unauthorized access to confidential data through SSRF. The vulnerability was discovered and reported to the Acronis security team, who investigated and found no signs of exploitation.
1721098: An out-of-bounds access vulnerability was discovered in the .netrc parser of Curl. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to cause an application crash and potentially other consequences. The vulnerability was caused by a loop in the parser that did not properly handle non-space characters in the .netrc file.
1722065: A double-free vulnerability was found in curl related to HTTP proxies, which could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service.
1723445: A vulnerability was discovered where no rate limiting was implemented for account removal requests on a website. This allowed an attacker to send a large number of automated account removal requests without limitation, which could have led to users' accounts being removed without consent. The issue was addressed by adding precautions such as reCAPTCHAs and request limits to prevent exploitation of the system through brute force tactics.
1724464: The `cd` (check disabled) flag in DNS-over-HTTPS JSON API requests to cloudflare-dns.com was not properly validated, allowing DNSSEC verification to be bypassed despite setting the flag value to `0` or `false`. The vulnerability was fixed by the Cloudflare Engineering team.
1726445: A critical vulnerability was found in gsi-openssh-server 7.9p1 on Fedora, allowing anyone to log in to the system with an existing user even if they provide an incorrect password, if PermitPAMUserChange is set to yes in the sshd_config file. The vulnerability could lead to a privilege escalation attack and impact confidentiality, integrity, and availability. The issue was discovered in February 2019 and is identified as CVE-2019-7639.
1727044: A vulnerability existed in the Gratipay migration tool of Liberapay that allowed an attacker to retrieve the primary email address of any user on the site without authorization. By inputting the username of the target user, the attacker could access the email address through the website's HTML response. The vulnerability was caused by the website automatically displaying the email address of the existing account, despite the current user's lack of authorization to view that information.
1727424: A security vulnerability was found in the password creation process of a website, where there was no limit on the length of passwords. This could potentially lead to a Denial of Service (DoS) attack by overwhelming the server with lengthy passwords.
1730660: HSTS checks were bypassed in some cases due to the conversion of certain characters in Internationalized Domain Names (IDN) to a period character. This vulnerability allowed an attacker to bypass HSTS protection and potentially conduct man-in-the-middle attacks.
1735586: WordPress users' personal information was disclosed through the REST API, allowing attackers to collect usernames and potentially use them in brute force attacks. The vulnerability was caused by the file v2/users being enabled, which allowed anyone to view active usernames. A fix was provided to hide the users list and return a 404 error instead.
1735622: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found in the chatbot feature of a website, allowing an attacker to execute malicious scripts in the victim's browser by sending a specially crafted link. This could potentially compromise the user and allow the attacker to perform actions in the application on their behalf.
1736432: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a system host, allowing an attacker to execute remote code on a victim's browser and potentially steal sensitive information. The vulnerability could be triggered using the "project" parameter and a bypass was possible despite the presence of a WAF.
1736433: A reflected XSS vulnerability was found on a system host, allowing an attacker to execute remote code on a victim's browser and potentially steal sensitive information. The vulnerability was triggered through the "plot" parameter and a WAF was in place but could be bypassed.
1745766: A vulnerability in Nextcloud allowed users to download preview images and first pages of shared documents even if the "Allow download" permission was disabled, potentially leaking sensitive information.
1747146: In a ████████ application, an authentication bypass vulnerability was discovered that allowed an attacker to access the Tiny filemanager using default credentials. The vulnerability enabled the attacker to perform actions such as modifying, uploading, and deleting files on the system.
1752146: Libcurl versions 7.7 to 7.85.0 were affected by a vulnerability that could cause the library to erroneously use the read callback to ask for data to send, even when the POSTFIELDS option had been set, if the same handle previously was used to issue a PUT request which used that callback. This could cause the application to misbehave and either send off the wrong data or use memory after free or similar in the subsequent POST request. The vulnerability was fixed in version 7.86.0.
1753224: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-35260) was discovered in curl versions 7.84.0 to 7.85.0 that could allow a malicious user to cause a denial-of-service attack by providing a custom netrc file to an application or otherwise affecting its contents. The flaw was caused by an out-of-bounds access in the .netrc parser, which could cause a segfault or similar outcome. The issue was fixed in curl version 7.86.0.
1753226: Curl versions 7.77.0 to 7.85.0 were affected by a vulnerability that allowed HSTS bypass via IDN. The flaw could be exploited to trick curl into using HTTP instead of HTTPS, even when instructed to use HTTPS directly. The vulnerability was fixed in version 7.86.0.
1755083: A vulnerability (CVE-2022-43551) was discovered that allowed for bypassing HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) checks via Internationalized Domain Names (IDN). Any character in the IDN that converts to a period character would bypass HSTS checks, due to the hostname before IDN conversion being used when writing to the HSTS cache. This could allow an attacker to intercept or modify traffic that was intended to be sent over HTTPS.
1758132: An insecure handling of create link tags in a function called `autolink` found in `7Bmt.af733e428f9f986dfc96.js` in Khan Academy allowed for an XSS attack. A specially crafted postmessage could abuse this vulnerability. The attack could steal user data and manipulate user accounts.
1761505: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability was found in the suggest tag functionality of an application, allowing an attacker to inject and execute malicious JavaScript code in the victim's browser. This could potentially compromise the user's system and allow the attacker to steal sensitive information. The vulnerability has since been fixed.
1764858: A use-after-free vulnerability was discovered in libcurl, which could allow an attacker to access and use already freed heap-memory for read and write operations. The vulnerability was reported by Trail of Bits.
1767439: An exposed log file at https://nextcloud.com/wp-content/debug.log allowed for full internal path disclosure, revealing sensitive information about the website's internal structure and potentially aiding attackers in future attacks.
1767771: A vulnerability was discovered that allowed an attacker to take over any subdomain of the zyrosite.com domain. The vulnerability was due to an issue in the `/v3/publish/connect-domain-hostinger` API endpoint, which allowed an attacker to connect their site to any subdomain of the zyrosite.com domain. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to take over any subdomain of the zyrosite.com domain.
1773895: A vulnerability in the UI of Apache Airflow allowed an attacker to view unmasked secrets in rendered template values for tasks that were not executed, affecting versions prior to 2.3.1.
1777077: The subdomain learn2.khanacademy.org was vulnerable to S3 bucket takeover as it was pointed to Amazon S3, but no bucket with that name was registered. This allowed anyone to sign up for Amazon S3, claim the bucket as their own and serve any content, including malicious content, on the domain.
1781102: Insecure use of shell.openExternal() in Rocket.Chat-Desktop allowed for potential remote code execution. The vulnerability was present in the openInternalVideoChatWindow function and could be exploited through an XSS attack. The vulnerability required the internal video chat window to be disabled or a Mac App Store build to be used.
1782514: An open redirect vulnerability existed in the webserver's `/login` endpoint of Apache Airflow versions prior to 2.4.3, allowing unvalidated URL redirection during login, which could be exploited for phishing attacks.
1783015: A host header injection vulnerability was discovered on the Urban Company website, allowing access to multiple subdomains that should have been inaccessible. The vulnerability was exploited using Burp and Match and Replace rule, and allowed access to subdomains such as av.urbancompany.com, ims.urbancompany.com, and mesh.urbancompany.com. The impact of the vulnerability depended on the sensitivity of the information accessible through the subdomains.
1784999: A vulnerability was found in the WordPress REST API, which allowed anyone to view active usernames of WordPress users/authors, including personal information of employees/authors. The file v2/users was enabled, which gave attackers access to many usernames. The vulnerability was not resolved despite a previous report, and the impacted domain was advised to remove the file if it was not in use.
1785378: A vulnerability existed in the `.bash_prompt` file of the dotfiles repository due to the improper usage of the `PS1` environment variable in displaying the VCS information. A malicious repository with a crafted branch name could execute arbitrary commands when the current directory was changed to it. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by tricking the victim into entering a malicious directory.
1787810: A delimiter injection vulnerability was found in the Electron package `core.exportVariable`. Attackers could use a well-known delimiter to break out of a specific variable and assign values to other arbitrary variables, potentially modifying the path or other environment variables unintentionally. The vulnerability was assigned CVE-2022-35954 and impacted the security of the package. Users were advised to upgrade to `@actions/core v1.9.1` or ensure that any user input did not contain the delimiter before calling `core.exportVariable`.
1804128: Certain configurations of rails-html-sanitizer < 1.4.4 and Loofah are susceptible to a regular expression denial-of-service (ReDoS) vulnerability when attempting to sanitize certain SVG attributes, which may lead to excessive CPU resource consumption and a denial of service. The vulnerability has been fixed in rails-html-sanitizer >= 1.4.4 and Loofah.
